props.What it is: Feedback control measures the error between where a joint is and where it should be, and pushes in the direction that shrinks it. A PID controller does this with three terms: Proportional (push harder when far), Integral (fix a constant offset), Derivative (brake to avoid overshoot). Almost every motor in a robot runs some PID loop.
props.Prerequisites: High-school calculus; basic Python
props.Frontier state 2026: Mature; current practice is cascaded PID with feedforward and anti-windup, e.g. ros2_controllers PID controller exposes back-calculation anti-windup and feedforward, and PX4/Crazyflie multirotors run cascaded PID by default. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Åström & Murray (Feedback Systems), ros2_control maintainers, PX4, Bitcraze
props.Best resources: Feedback Systems (Åström & Murray, free PDF); Modern Robotics ch. 11 videos; python-control library

props.What it is: To control something you first write down how it moves: equations that say how the state (positions, velocities) changes when you apply forces. State-space form, x_dot = A x + B u, is the common language used by LQR, MPC and simulators.
props.Prerequisites: Linear algebra; ordinary differential equations
props.Frontier state 2026: Model-based control relies on fast rigid-body dynamics libraries with analytic derivatives (Pinocchio) and physics engines (MuJoCo, Drake); 2026 work identifies object parameters with differentiable simulation (RigPI). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: MIT (Tedrake), Inria/LAAS (Pinocchio), Google DeepMind (MuJoCo), Toyota Research Institute (Drake)
props.Best resources: Underactuated Robotics ch. 2-3 (MIT); Feedback Systems ch. 2-3; python-control docs

props.What it is: Stability asks whether a controlled robot settles down or starts shaking and diverging. Engineers check it with eigenvalues, Bode plots (how the system reacts to fast vs slow signals) and Lyapunov functions (an 'energy' that always decreases). It explains why too-high gains make a robot oscillate.
props.Prerequisites: Dynamic system modeling & state-space; complex numbers
props.Frontier state 2026: Classical theory is settled; active work uses Lyapunov and sums-of-squares certificates to verify learned or nonlinear controllers. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: MIT (Tedrake), Åström & Murray (Feedback Systems)
props.Best resources: Feedback Systems ch. 5, 9-10; Underactuated Robotics ch. 9 (Lyapunov analysis); Modern Robotics 11.2

props.What it is: A controller needs a smooth target to follow, not a jump. Trajectory generation turns 'go from A to B' into a time-stamped path that respects speed, acceleration and jerk limits (trapezoidal or S-curve profiles). Smooth targets mean less shaking and less wear.
props.Prerequisites: Basic calculus; Feedback control & PID
props.Frontier state 2026: Online jerk-limited time-optimal generation is a solved, open-source problem for state-to-state motions (Ruckig, MIT licence); research moves to learned movement primitives (2025-2026 survey). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Ruckig (pantor), ros2_controllers joint_trajectory_controller, PX4 jerk-limited setpoints
props.Best resources: Ruckig README and examples; Modern Robotics ch. 9; ros2_controllers JointTrajectoryController docs

props.What it is: Each arm joint must follow its trajectory despite gravity and the pull of the other links. Simple PD control works at low speed; adding gravity compensation and 'computed torque' (using the arm's dynamic model to cancel its own inertia) gives precise fast motion.
props.Prerequisites: Feedback control & PID; Dynamic system modeling & state-space; forward kinematics
props.Frontier state 2026: Standard textbook material (Modern Robotics ch. 11, Murray-Li-Sastry ch. 4); research platforms like Franka FR3 expose 1 kHz torque control so students can run their own laws. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Northwestern (Lynch), Franka Robotics, ros2_control community
props.Best resources: Modern Robotics ch. 11 (computed torque); Coursera Modern Robotics Course 4; Pinocchio examples

props.What it is: Real motors have friction, backlash and delays that no datasheet lists. System identification means running test motions, recording data and fitting a model to it; tuning then picks controller gains that work on that model. It is how you close the gap between simulation and the real robot.
props.Prerequisites: Dynamic system modeling & state-space; least squares regression
props.Frontier state 2026: Learned and hybrid models are mainstream: neural ODEs adapt mobile-robot dynamics online (AD-NODE, 2025) and VLM-seeded differentiable simulation identifies inertial/friction parameters (RigPI, 2026). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: ETH Zurich RSL, ODrive Robotics, research groups behind RigPI/AD-NODE
props.Best resources: python-control (system responses); ODrive controller tuning docs; Underactuated Robotics system-ID appendix

props.What it is: Instead of hand-tuning gains, you write down a cost (how bad errors and effort are) and let math find the best controller. The Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) does this for linear models in one function call, and is the classic way to balance a cart-pole or a drone.
props.Prerequisites: Dynamic system modeling & state-space; linear algebra
props.Frontier state 2026: LQR remains the default stabilizer around equilibria and inside iLQR-style MPC; Tedrake calls it 'likely the most important and influential result' in optimal control. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: MIT (Tedrake), Toyota Research Institute (Drake), python-control developers
props.Best resources: Underactuated Robotics ch. 8 (LQR); Feedback Systems ch. 7; python-control lqr()

props.What it is: MPC repeatedly solves a small optimization: 'given my model, what are the best next N commands?', applies the first one, then re-plans a few milliseconds later. It handles limits (max torque, obstacles) directly, which is why legged robots, drones and cars use it.
props.Prerequisites: Optimal control & LQR; basic numerical optimization
props.Frontier state 2026: Nonlinear MPC runs in real time with embedded solvers (acados, OCS2); 2026 work adds whole-body humanoid iLQR-MPC (arXiv 2611.04204), robust reduced-order MPC (CoRE-MPC) and GPU-accelerated robust adaptive MPC (A-SLS). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: acados team (Freiburg), ETH RSL (OCS2), CasADi team, do-mpc team
props.Best resources: acados docs and examples; CasADi docs; do-mpc tutorials; Underactuated Robotics trajectory optimization chapter
props.Sources:
https://docs.acados.org/
https://web.casadi.org/
https://www.do-mpc.com/en/latest/
https://github.com/leggedrobotics/ocs2
https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04204
https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19250
https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20925

props.What it is: Trajectory optimization finds a whole motion at once, for example the best swing-up of a pendulum or a jump, by minimizing cost subject to physics. Methods include direct collocation (optimize states and controls at sample points) and DDP/iLQR (iteratively improve a trajectory with local LQR).
props.Prerequisites: Optimal control & LQR; nonlinear optimization basics
props.Frontier state 2026: DDP-family solvers (Crocoddyl FDDP) and direct methods in Drake are standard; contact-implicit and differentiable-contact trajectory optimization is an active 2026 research area. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: LAAS-CNRS/Inria (Crocoddyl, Pinocchio), MIT/TRI (Drake), ETH RSL
props.Best resources: Underactuated Robotics ch. 10; Crocoddyl examples; Drake tutorials

props.What it is: Impedance control makes a robot behave like a virtual spring and damper: push it and it yields, let go and it returns. Admittance control is the mirror image for stiff position-controlled robots: it measures force and turns it into motion. These are the control laws behind hand-guiding, safe contact and HRI (contact-rich manipulation tasks themselves are covered in the Manipulation branch).
props.Prerequisites: Joint-space control of robot arms; Feedback control & PID
props.Frontier state 2026: Mature on torque-controlled arms (FR3 joint torque sensors, 1 kHz); 2026 research learns stiffness and equilibrium point from demonstrations (Impedance Cloning) instead of raw trajectories. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Franka Robotics, ros2_control maintainers, Impedance Cloning authors
props.Best resources: Modern Robotics 11.6-11.7; ros2_controllers admittance_controller docs; libfranka examples

props.What it is: Rather than commanding each joint, task-space control commands what matters: 'hand here, keep balance, don't hit joint limits'. Whole-body control stacks many such tasks and solves a quadratic program (QP) every millisecond to find torques that satisfy them all by priority. Humanoids and legged robots rely on it.
props.Prerequisites: Joint-space control of robot arms; Jacobians; quadratic programming
props.Frontier state 2026: QP-based TSID-style controllers (TSID, ProxSuite, OSQP) coexist with learned whole-body policies; RSS 2025 accepted papers include several learned humanoid whole-body controllers (e.g. AMO, LangWBC). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: LAAS-CNRS (TSID), Inria Willow (ProxSuite), ETH RSL
props.Best resources: TSID repository and notebooks; ETH Robot Dynamics lecture; Pinocchio docs

props.What it is: An underactuated robot has fewer motors than ways it can move, like a cart balancing a pole, a ballbot or a walking robot. You must use the dynamics (falling, swinging) instead of fighting them: energy shaping to swing up, LQR to balance at the top.
props.Prerequisites: Optimal control & LQR; Dynamic system modeling & state-space
props.Frontier state 2026: Textbook problems are solved (MIT 6.832); 2026 work combines MPC and control barrier functions for ballbot navigation, validated in MuJoCo simulation (Safe-Ballbot). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: MIT (Tedrake, 6.832), Safe-Ballbot authors, safe-control-gym maintainers
props.Best resources: Underactuated Robotics ch. 2-3 and lecture videos; MIT OCW 6.832; safe-control-gym cart-pole

props.What it is: A wheeled robot must follow a planned path while its wheels can only roll forward and turn. Controllers such as pure pursuit (aim at a point ahead on the path) and MPPI (sample many possible paths and pick the best) turn the path into wheel speed commands.
props.Prerequisites: Feedback control & PID; 2D geometry
props.Frontier state 2026: Nav2 ships Regulated Pure Pursuit and an MPPI controller as standard ROS 2 plugins; research adds learned adaptive dynamics (AD-NODE). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Open Navigation / Nav2 maintainers, ros2_control (diff_drive_controller)
props.Best resources: Nav2 controller plugin READMEs; ros2_controllers wheeled-robot controllers; MPPI paper

props.What it is: A drone has no stable resting state in the air, so a fast control stack runs constantly: an inner loop holds the attitude rate, outer loops hold attitude, velocity and position. Learning it on a 29 g Crazyflie or in PX4 simulation shows cascaded control in action.
props.Prerequisites: Feedback control & PID; 3D rotations
props.Frontier state 2026: Cascaded PID remains the default (PX4, Crazyflie); Crazyflie also ships Mellinger, INDI, Brescianini and Lee controllers; RL end-to-end RPM control transferred after 18 s of laptop training (Learning to Fly in Seconds); 2026 nonlinear MPC planners for agile flight (NMPP). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: PX4 / Dronecode, Bitcraze, Neural Lander authors (Shi, Chung et al.), Learning to Fly in Seconds authors
props.Best resources: PX4 controller diagrams; Crazyflie controllers docs; Underactuated Robotics quadrotor section

props.What it is: Visual servoing closes the control loop through a camera: the robot moves until what it sees matches a target image or target object pose. It removes the need for perfect calibration because the error is measured directly in the image.
props.Prerequisites: Feedback control & PID; camera geometry basics; Joint-space control of robot arms
props.Frontier state 2026: Classic IBVS/PBVS are packaged in ViSP (Inria); 2026 work replaces handcrafted features with pretrained visual geometry models for high-precision PBVS (VGM-VS). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Inria Rainbow team (ViSP), Lagadic community
props.Best resources: ViSP tutorials and docs; Modern Robotics (kinematics); VGM-VS paper

props.What it is: Real robots are nonlinear and their parameters change (a payload, a worn motor). Nonlinear methods like feedback linearization use the full model; robust control guarantees behavior for a range of errors; adaptive control updates the model online while running.
props.Prerequisites: Stability & frequency-domain analysis; Optimal control & LQR
props.Frontier state 2026: Learning-aware robust adaptive MPC on GPU (A-SLS, 2026) and learned-residual dynamics (Neural Lander) show the merge of adaptive control and ML. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: A-SLS authors, Neural Lander authors, Murray/Li/Sastry (textbook)
props.Best resources: Murray-Li-Sastry book; Underactuated Robotics (partial feedback linearization); A-SLS paper

props.What it is: Instead of solving equations, sampling-based MPC simulates thousands of random command sequences in parallel on a GPU, scores them, and keeps a weighted best. It works even with contacts and non-smooth physics, and can make a simulated humanoid or quadruped move with no training.
props.Prerequisites: Model predictive control (MPC); GPU/JAX programming
props.Frontier state 2026: MuJoCo MPC (predictive sampling, 2022), Hydrax (MPPI/CEM on JAX/MJX GPUs) and DIAL-MPC (diffusion-style annealing, full-order torque-level legged MPC; ICRA 2025 best-paper finalist per its repo) bring training-free whole-body control to sim and real quadrupeds. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Google DeepMind (MJPC), CMU LeCAR Lab (DIAL-MPC), Hydrax authors, Nav2 (MPPI)
props.Best resources: MuJoCo MPC repository; Hydrax README; DIAL-MPC paper and code

props.What it is: A safety filter sits between any controller (even a neural network) and the motors and minimally edits commands that would break a safety rule, like 'stay 20 cm from the wall'. Control barrier functions (CBFs) express those rules mathematically and are solved as a tiny QP every step.
props.Prerequisites: Optimal control & LQR; quadratic programming; Stability & frequency-domain analysis
props.Frontier state 2026: CBF-QPs are widely used (Ames et al. survey) and combined with MPC for ballbot navigation (Safe-Ballbot, 2026, validated in MuJoCo simulation); safe learning surveys (Brunke et al.; 2024 survey) frame filters for learned policies; safety filters appear in RSS 2025 papers. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Ames et al. (CBF survey authors), Schoellig group (safe-control-gym), Safe-Ballbot authors
props.Best resources: Ames et al. 'Control Barrier Functions: Theory and Applications'; safe-control-gym; Brunke et al. survey

props.What it is: Here machine learning improves or replaces parts of the controller: learning the dynamics model, learning a residual correction on top of a classic controller, or training a reinforcement-learning policy that outputs motor commands directly. The challenge is keeping it stable and safe on real hardware.
props.Prerequisites: Feedback control & PID; reinforcement learning basics; Model predictive control (MPC)
props.Frontier state 2026: Residual RL (Johannink et al.), learned residual dynamics (Neural Lander) and fast sim-to-real RL for quadrotors (18 s training) are established; 2026 work learns impedance parameters (Impedance Cloning) and adaptive dynamics (AD-NODE). General robot-learning policies are covered in the Robot learning branch. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Schoellig group (safe-learning survey, safe-control-gym), Neural Lander authors, Residual RL authors (Johannink, Bahl et al.)
props.Best resources: Brunke et al. safe-learning survey; safe-control-gym; Residual RL paper

props.What it is: The basic rules of electricity a robot runs on: voltage, current, resistance (Ohm's law), power, and how to read a schematic. You use a multimeter and breadboard to check that a circuit does what you think before you plug in a motor.
props.Prerequisites: High-school physics; none in robotics.
props.Frontier state 2026: Stable knowledge; free browser circuit simulators (Falstad, Wokwi) let students learn before buying parts.
props.Key players: Arduino, SparkFun, Adafruit (education); Texas Instruments app notes
props.Best resources: Arduino Learn hub; SparkFun & Adafruit tutorials; Falstad circuit simulator

props.What it is: A microcontroller (MCU) is a small computer on one chip that reads sensors and controls outputs such as motor-driver signals. Bare-metal firmware runs without an operating system; other MCU applications use an RTOS or an interpreter such as MicroPython.
props.Prerequisites: C programming; Electronics fundamentals for robots.
props.Frontier state 2026: Available platforms include ESP32-S3 (dual-core 240 MHz, Wi-Fi/BLE and vector instructions), Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (RP2350), Teensy 4.1 (Cortex-M7 600 MHz) and STM32 devices. Arduino UNO Q pairs a Linux MPU with an STM32U585 MCU running Zephyr. Embassy provides an asynchronous embedded Rust framework.
props.Key players: Espressif, Raspberry Pi, STMicroelectronics, PJRC, Arduino, Rust Embedded WG
props.Best resources: Cornell ECE 4760 (RP2350, free lectures); PlatformIO; The Embedded Rust Book
props.Sources: https://www.espressif.com/en/products/socs/esp32-s3 ; https://www.pjrc.com/store/teensy41.html ; https://docs.arduino.cc/hardware/uno-q/ ; https://ece4760.github.io/ ; https://platformio.org/ ; https://docs.rust-embedded.org/book/ ; https://embassy.dev/ ; https://www.raspberrypi.com/products/raspberry-pi-pico-2/

props.What it is: Buses are the ways chips and boards exchange data: UART is simple serial, I2C and SPI connect local peripherals, and CAN / CAN-FD support robust multi-node communication. A protocol, its physical wiring and the supported frame format must all match before devices can communicate.
props.Prerequisites: Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware.
props.Frontier state 2026: CiA describes Classical CAN, CAN-FD and CAN XL as three CAN generations. moteus uses CAN-FD; ODrive Pro/S1 support it with suitable firmware and configuration. ESP32-S3 TWAI supports Classical CAN only and requires an external transceiver; use an external CAN-FD controller plus a compatible transceiver for FD traffic.
props.Key players: CAN in Automation (CiA), Bosch, Espressif, SparkFun
props.Best resources: SparkFun I2C tutorial; CiA CAN knowledge pages; ESP-IDF TWAI docs

props.What it is: Smart servos such as Feetech STS and ROBOTIS DYNAMIXEL combine a motor, gearbox and controller. Compatible servos can share a daisy-chained serial bus and return feedback; SO-101 is one low-cost arm built this way.
props.Prerequisites: Communication buses (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN).
props.Frontier state 2026: SO-101 uses six STS3215 servos per arm, including the gripper. The follower uses 1/345 gearing; the leader uses three 1/147, two 1/191 and one 1/345 servo. ROBOTIS documents DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 for compatible servo models.
props.Key players: Feetech, ROBOTIS, The Robot Studio, Hugging Face
props.Best resources: LeRobot SO-101 docs; Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 e-manual

props.What it is: A microcontroller pin can't power a motor; a motor driver (H-bridge, MOSFET stage) switches the battery current on and off very fast (PWM) to control speed and torque. This node covers brushed DC, stepper and the basics of brushless (BLDC) drivers, current sensing and heat.
props.Prerequisites: Electronics fundamentals for robots; Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware.
props.Frontier state 2026: Integrated driver ICs (e.g. TI DRV88xx) cover small robots; high-power robot joints use dedicated BLDC controllers.
props.Key players: Texas Instruments, Infineon, STMicroelectronics, ODrive Robotics
props.Best resources: TI DRV8833 datasheet and TI motor-driver app notes

props.What it is: Brushless motors are used in many legged robots and drones. Field-oriented control (FOC) uses motor angle and current information to control torque smoothly. Ready-made controllers and libraries let you learn FOC without first designing a power stage.
props.Prerequisites: Motor drivers & power electronics; basic control (PID).
props.Frontier state 2026: Katz's 2018 MIT thesis describes a low-cost modular actuator for dynamic robots. moteus and SimpleFOC publish open-source control code; current ODrive S1/Pro firmware is not publicly available, unlike the legacy ODrive repository. CubeMars and RobStride sell integrated actuators; protocol and ratings depend on the model.
props.Key players: ODrive Robotics, mjbots, SimpleFOC community, CubeMars, RobStride, MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab
props.Best resources: SimpleFOC docs; moteus reference manual; Katz MIT thesis 'A low cost modular actuator for dynamic robots'
props.Sources: https://simplefoc.com/ ; https://github.com/simplefoc/Arduino-FOC ; https://odriverobotics.com/ ; https://github.com/odriverobotics/ODrive ; https://github.com/mjbots/moteus ; https://github.com/mjbots/moteus/blob/main/docs/reference.md ; https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/118671 ; https://www.cubemars.com/ ; https://robstride.com/

props.What it is: Robots read the world through encoders, IMUs, current and force sensors. This node is the electrical side: ADCs, pull-ups, filtering noise, sampling rates and timestamps, so the data your AI model gets is clean.
props.Prerequisites: Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware; Communication buses (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN).
props.Frontier state 2026: No specific 2026 change established. Current controller examples expose encoder and current feedback; sampling, filtering and timing remain application-dependent engineering tasks.
props.Key players: Adafruit and SparkFun (education and interfaces); Cornell ECE 4760 (signal processing labs); ODrive Robotics (controller feedback)
props.Best resources: Cornell ECE 4760 filtering, sampling and encoder examples; SparkFun I2C tutorial; ODrive controller documentation

props.What it is: A robot needs an energy source, suitable voltage regulation, protected wiring and a way to handle faults. Battery management systems monitor conditions such as cell voltage, temperature and current. Beginners should start with a current-limited bench supply or a protected commercial pack, not assemble loose lithium cells.
props.Prerequisites: Electronics fundamentals for robots.
props.Frontier state 2026: No specific 2026 breakthrough established here. TI BQ76952 is an example of a 3-to-16-cell monitor/protector; Battery University explains how temperature, charge level and discharge depth affect lithium-battery life.
props.Key players: Battery University (Cadex), Texas Instruments
props.Best resources: Battery University BU-808 for cell care; TI BQ76952 product documentation for monitoring and protection concepts

props.What it is: Bigger robots pair the microcontroller with a small Linux computer (Raspberry Pi, Jetson, Arduino UNO Q) that runs cameras, ROS 2 and AI models, while the MCU handles hard real-time motor loops. Knowing how to split work between them is a key design skill.
props.Prerequisites: Linux basics; Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware.
props.Frontier state 2026: Arduino UNO Q combines a Qualcomm QRB2210 running Debian with an STM32U585 running Zephyr. Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ offers Hailo-8L (13 TOPS) or Hailo-8 (26 TOPS) acceleration for Raspberry Pi 5; the host board and cooling are additional hardware.
props.Key players: Raspberry Pi, NVIDIA, Arduino, Qualcomm
props.Best resources: Arduino UNO Q docs; Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ product info; NVIDIA Jetson docs

props.What it is: Motor and balance controllers need predictable timing, for example a loop every 1 ms. An RTOS such as FreeRTOS or Zephyr, or real-time Linux with PREEMPT_RT, helps reduce scheduling delays but cannot by itself guarantee deadlines. You must measure jitter and validate worst-case execution, interrupt load and failure handling.
props.Prerequisites: Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware; OS concepts (threads, interrupts).
props.Frontier state 2026: PREEMPT_RT was merged into mainline Linux 6.12 (Nov 2024) after ~20 years; Zephyr is used by Arduino UNO Q for its MCU side.
props.Key players: FreeRTOS (AWS), Zephyr Project (Linux Foundation), Linux kernel RT maintainers
props.Best resources: Lee & Seshia 'Introduction to Embedded Systems' (free, Berkeley EECS149); FreeRTOS and Zephyr docs

props.What it is: ros2_control connects ROS 2 controllers to hardware interfaces. micro-ROS provides a resource-constrained ROS 2 client on a microcontroller, typically communicating with an agent on a larger computer. Shared interfaces can support simulation and hardware, but drivers and timing still need testing.
props.Prerequisites: Embedded Linux & companion computers; ROS 2 basics.
props.Frontier state 2026: The rolling ros2_control documentation includes Embedded Integration and is a development-version reference. micro.ros.org redirects visitors to micro.vulcanexus.org; the ESP-IDF component supports ESP32-family boards. Select documentation matching the ROS distribution used by the lab.
props.Key players: ros-controls community, eProsima (micro-ROS/Vulcanexus), Open Robotics

props.What it is: EtherCAT is an industrial Ethernet fieldbus designed for short communication cycles and precise synchronization of devices such as motor drives. SOEM is a source-available EtherCAT master library usable from a suitable host; actual timing depends on the complete system.
props.Prerequisites: Communication buses (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN); Real-time OS & real-time control loops.
props.Frontier state 2026: Originally developed by Beckhoff and specified in IEC 61158. ETG documents short cycle times and distributed-clock synchronization; these design capabilities are not guaranteed benchmark results for an arbitrary Linux setup.
props.Key players: Beckhoff, EtherCAT Technology Group, Open EtherCAT Society

props.What it is: Designing your own printed circuit board replaces a fragile nest of jumper wires with a clean, reliable board: schematic capture, layout, ordering from a fab. KiCad is the free, professional-grade tool.
props.Prerequisites: Electronics fundamentals for robots; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning.
props.Frontier state 2026: KiCad 10.x is current (10.0.8 released Oct 2026).
props.Key players: KiCad project

props.What it is: Running neural networks on the robot itself instead of the cloud: from tiny models on microcontrollers (TinyML) to vision accelerators (Hailo) to GPU modules (Jetson) that can run VLAs. Choosing the chip sets your latency, power and battery life.
props.Prerequisites: Embedded Linux & companion computers; deep learning basics.
props.Frontier state 2026: NVIDIA launched the Jetson AGX Thor developer kit in August 2025 from US$3,499; Jetson Thor specifications list up to 2070 FP4 TFLOPS, 128 GB and 40-130 W. Orin Nano Super is rated up to 67 TOPS; Hailo-8 up to 26 TOPS. Precision, model support and end-to-end latency differ, so these figures are not directly comparable. LiteRT for Microcontrollers and Edge Impulse support smaller MCU-scale models.
props.Key players: NVIDIA, Hailo, Google (LiteRT), Edge Impulse, Espressif
props.Best resources: NVIDIA Jetson pages; LiteRT for Microcontrollers guide; Edge Impulse docs

props.What it is: Simulators and emulators let you test firmware against virtual peripherals before connecting a physical circuit. Wokwi provides browser simulation and Renode emulates embedded systems. Hardware-in-the-loop is a separate setup using real hardware connected to a test environment; it is not automatically supplied by an emulator.
props.Prerequisites: Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware.
props.Frontier state 2026: Renode is an open-source embedded-system simulation framework from Antmicro. Wokwi supports devices including ESP32, Arduino and Pi Pico, with browser access and separate paid integrations; check the chosen target and plan before using it in CI.
props.Key players: Antmicro, Wokwi, PlatformIO

knowledge.name: Electrical safety & functional safety for robots

props.What it is: Safety engineering identifies hazards and designs a controlled response to faults, using measures such as guarding, limits, watchdogs and emergency stops. Simply cutting motor power can let a gravity-loaded arm fall, so the safe stopping method depends on the mechanism and risk assessment. A student prototype is not a certified safety system and needs competent review before public use.
props.Prerequisites: Motor drivers & power electronics; Batteries & power distribution.
props.Frontier state 2026: ISO 13849-1:2023 is edition 4 (April 2023), covering methodology for safety-related control-system design and integration. The public catalogue does not establish the safety functions or performance level needed for a particular robot; the full standard and application-specific requirements need specialist assessment.
props.Key players: ISO (standards publisher); competent machinery-safety engineers for application assessment
props.Best resources: ISO 13849-1:2023 public abstract; full standard for qualified design work (not replaced by a web summary)

aliases: Electrical safety & functional safety for robots

knowledge.name: Open-source actuator & electronics stacks for legged/humanoid robots

props.What it is: Open robot designs show how actuators, power, wiring and embedded computers fit together. Berkeley Humanoid Lite uses BLDC actuators with 3D-printed gearboxes, while Open Duck Mini v2 uses a different, smart-servo-based stack. Reproducing either requires integration and safety work, not just downloading a policy.
props.Prerequisites: BLDC motor control & field-oriented control (FOC); Communication buses (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN); Batteries & power distribution.
props.Frontier state 2026: Berkeley Humanoid Lite (2025) publishes hardware and software and reports hardware cost below US$5,000 using U.S. market prices. Open Duck Mini v2 publishes a roughly 42 cm biped and a target BOM below US$400. These are source-reported parts estimates, not delivered French lab budgets or guaranteed build outcomes.
props.Key players: UC Berkeley (Hybrid Robotics), Open Duck Mini community, MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab, mjbots
props.Best resources: Berkeley Humanoid Lite site/paper; Open Duck Mini repo

aliases: Open-source actuator & electronics stacks for legged/humanoid robots

props.What it is: Before a robot works near people, engineers list what could hurt someone (hazards), estimate how bad and how likely it is, and add measures until the remaining risk is acceptable. International standards give the vocabulary and method: ISO 12100 for machines in general, ISO 10218 for industrial robots, ISO 13482 for personal-care robots.
props.Prerequisites: None for reading; basic notion of how a robot arm moves helps.
props.Frontier state 2026: ISO 10218-1:2025 (Edition 3) and ISO 10218-2:2025 (Edition 2) were published in 2025-02. ISO/TS 15066:2016 (collaborative robots) was confirmed in 2022 and remains current, but ISO lists it as "to be revised" and to be replaced by ISO/AWI 15066-1 (under development). ISO 12100:2010 is expected to be replaced by ISO/DIS 12100.3, and ISO 13482:2014 is also marked as expected to be replaced. Full texts are paid; only catalogue abstracts were read.
props.Key players: ISO (standards publisher); robot makers that document certified safety functions, e.g. Universal Robots
props.Best resources: ISO catalogue pages for ISO 12100, 10218-1/-2, 13482 ; Bartneck et al., Human-Robot Interaction: An Introduction (free site)

props.What it is: A collaborative robot (cobot) shares space with people. Standards describe ways to make this safe, including power and force limiting (contact is allowed but forces stay below limits) and speed and separation monitoring (the robot slows or stops as a person gets closer). Which mode fits comes from the risk assessment, not from the robot label.
props.Prerequisites: Robot safety standards & risk assessment
props.Frontier state 2026: ISO/TS 15066:2016 supplements ISO 10218-1/-2 for collaborative industrial robot systems and does not apply to non-industrial robots. Research cited in 2024-2026 papers uses ISO 10218-2:2025 contact thresholds; one 2026 paper reports that the blunt-impact data does not cover edged or pointed collisions.
props.Key players: Universal Robots (configurable safety limits, always-active power and force limiting); Franka Robotics; CTU Prague and TU Munich research groups (from opened papers)
props.Best resources: ISO/TS 15066 abstract ; arXiv 1908.03046 (unified SSM + PFL) ; arXiv 1805.07256

props.What it is: Human-robot interaction (HRI) studies how people and robots communicate and work together. Because "it felt natural" is not evidence, HRI uses user studies: questionnaires, behaviour measurements and sometimes physiological signals, with a clear protocol and statistics. Perceived safety (whether people feel safe) is measured separately from physical safety.
props.Prerequisites: Basic statistics
props.Frontier state 2026: The ACM/IEEE HRI conference ran its 21st edition (HRI 2026, Edinburgh, March 16-19, 2026) and announces Santa Clara for the next one. A survey lists questionnaires, physiological measurements, behavioural assessment and direct input devices to assess perceived safety.
props.Key players: ACM/IEEE HRI conference community; Bartneck et al. (textbook authors); Furhat Robotics (research platform)
props.Best resources: Human-Robot Interaction: An Introduction (book site) ; free edX/UCx HRI Professional Certificate ; arXiv 2105.14499 (perceived safety survey)

knowledge.name: Human detection & body-pose tracking for HRI

props.What it is: To react to people, a robot must first see them: where they are and how their body is posed. Pose estimators output keypoints (joints like wrists and shoulders) from a camera image, which later layers turn into distances, gestures or safety zones.
props.Prerequisites: Python; basic computer vision
props.Frontier state 2026: Off-the-shelf models run in real time: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker tracks 33 3D body landmarks and runs in the browser via WebAssembly; Ultralytics documents YOLO26 pose models pretrained on COCO keypoints. Research uses RGB-D cameras, lidar or on-robot ranging sensors for separation distance. None of these camera models is safety-rated.
props.Key players: Google (MediaPipe); Ultralytics; robotics labs using RGB-D/lidar for HRC distance
props.Best resources: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker docs ; Ultralytics pose docs ; arXiv 1810.04953 (RGB-D separation distance)

aliases: Human detection & body-pose tracking for HRI

props.What it is: Speed and separation monitoring means continuously measuring the distance between robot and human and lowering the robot speed (or stopping) so it can always stop before contact. Building it needs sensors, a distance computation between robot links and the person, and a speed-scaling rule.
props.Prerequisites: Collaborative operation modes (cobots); Human detection & body-pose tracking for HRI
props.Frontier state 2026: Research prototypes use time-of-flight sensor arrays on robot links, RGB-D cameras and 3D lidar; a 2025 study compares neural networks for learning safety speed reduction and a 2026 paper sizes protective zones from operator presence data. These are research results, not certified safety functions.
props.Key players: Research labs publishing on SSM (from opened arXiv papers); industrial safety-sensor vendors (not researched)

knowledge.name: Collision detection & reaction (power and force limiting)

props.What it is: If contact cannot be avoided, the robot must notice a collision (for example from joint torques or a sensitive skin) and react, such as stopping or becoming compliant. Power and force limiting keeps contact forces and pressures below thresholds that depend on the body region.
props.Prerequisites: Collaborative operation modes (cobots); basic robot dynamics
props.Frontier state 2026: Recent work makes thresholds adaptive: per-link effective mass with a UR10e and AIRSKIN skin (2024), reachability-based shields with formal guarantees (SARA shield, 2024), and injury databases extended to shearing contacts (2026). Low-cost smart servos are not designed or certified for this.
props.Key players: Universal Robots; Franka Robotics; CTU Prague (Hoffmann group, adaptive sensitivity); TU Munich (SARA shield)

aliases: Collision detection & reaction (power and force limiting)

props.What it is: In shared control, a human gives commands (joystick, teleoperation) and the robot blends them with its own autonomy, for example to help a person with motor impairments grasp a cup. The robot must infer what the human wants and decide how much to assist.
props.Prerequisites: Basic teleoperation; Python
props.Frontier state 2026: Deep RL can learn shared autonomy without assuming known goals (2018). 2026 papers explore legible shared autonomy (robot motion reveals its belief), capability-aware arbitration and blended shared control inside interactive imitation learning.
props.Key players: UC Berkeley (Reddy, Dragan, Levine); HRI and RSS communities

props.What it is: Kinesthetic teaching means a person physically moves the robot by hand to show a task, and the robot records the motion. It needs the robot to be compliant (it yields when pushed) and to compensate its own weight so it is easy and safe to guide.
props.Prerequisites: Collaborative operation modes (cobots); joint torque or current sensing basics
props.Frontier state 2026: 2024-2026 papers add mixed-reality feedback, observer-based hand-guiding with active support, force guidance and tactile data (KineDex) to kinesthetic teaching, and use it as a demonstration source for imitation and RL.
props.Key players: Franka Robotics (FCI research interface); research labs (from opened papers)
props.Best resources: Franka Control Interface docs ; arXiv 2409.02305 ; arXiv 2608.10847

props.What it is: A handover is passing an object between a robot and a person. It has a pre-handover phase (agreeing where and when, often implicitly) and a physical exchange that ends when the giver fully releases the object.
props.Prerequisites: Human detection & body-pose tracking for HRI; basic grasping
props.Frontier state 2026: Simulation benchmarks exist for human-to-robot (HandoverSim, 2022) and robot-to-human handovers (R2HandoverSim, 2026); 2025 work learns dexterous handovers.
props.Key players: Monash/QUT authors of the handover review; NVIDIA-affiliated HandoverSim authors (not verified as organizations)

props.What it is: Legible motion makes the robot intent obvious early, for example reaching in an exaggerated arc so a person guesses the target sooner. Predictable motion is what people expect; Dragan et al. showed the two are different and can conflict.
props.Prerequisites: Basic trajectory planning
props.Frontier state 2026: Legibility is extended to cluttered scenes, service-robot local planners (Legibot), comparisons with body-language cues (2026) and hallway navigation studies.
props.Key players: CMU (Dragan, Lee, Srinivasa 2013); HRI community
props.Best resources: Dragan et al., Legibility and Predictability of Robot Motion (HRI 2013) ; arXiv 2404.05100 ; arXiv 2604.03451

props.What it is: A mobile robot among people must reach its goal while respecting personal space, not cutting through groups and staying predictable. Evaluating this is hard because it depends on how humans perceive the robot.
props.Prerequisites: Basic mobile navigation (ROS 2 Nav2)
props.Frontier state 2026: A 2023 multi-author paper proposes principles and guidelines for evaluating social navigation. ROS 2 tools such as HuNavSim (2.0 in 2025, wrappers for Gazebo, Isaac Sim and Webots) and Arena 4.0/5.0 provide human simulation and benchmarking; 2024-2026 work adds LLM-based scenario generation and reasoning.
props.Key players: Universidad Pablo de Olavide (HuNavSim); Arena-Rosnav team; Google and academic co-authors of the guidelines
props.Sources:
https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16740
https://github.com/robotics-upo/hunav_sim
https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01303
https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12471
https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11220
https://docs.nav2.org/rolling/

props.What it is: Robots can now talk: speech recognition turns voice into text, a language model decides what to say or do, and the robot answers with voice, gestures and head motion. Timing (turn-taking, interruptions) and matching gestures to speech are what make it feel natural.
props.Prerequisites: Python; LLM APIs
props.Frontier state 2026: Open speech recognition (Whisper, MIT license) and LLMs make prototypes quick. 2026 papers address full-duplex interaction with interruptible motion (MIRA) and co-speech gesture generation for humanoids. Reachy Mini (Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face) is sold as an open-source HRI robot, Lite version listed at $399 plus taxes and shipping.
props.Key players: Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face (Reachy Mini, Paris); Furhat Robotics; Google DeepMind (Gemini Robotics)
props.Best resources: Reachy Mini blog and SDK ; Whisper repo ; arXiv 2404.00938 (LLMs for socially assistive HRI)

props.What it is: To move safely and helpfully, robots predict where people will walk or reach next, a few seconds ahead. Methods range from simple physics-like models (social forces) to deep networks trained on trajectory datasets.
props.Prerequisites: Human detection & body-pose tracking for HRI; basic ML
props.Frontier state 2026: Trajectron++ (ECCV 2020, MIT license) is a reference open model; 2023 work revisits the Social Force Model for low-compute prediction; 2026 papers target prediction specifically for human-robot collaboration.
props.Key players: Stanford ASL (Trajectron++); HRC research groups

knowledge.name: Robotics regulation & compliance in the EU

props.What it is: Selling or deploying a robot in Europe means following laws, not just standards. The new Machinery Regulation replaces the old Machinery Directive, and the AI Act adds rules for AI systems, including AI used as a safety component of products such as machinery.
props.Prerequisites: Robot safety standards & risk assessment
props.Frontier state 2026: Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 14 January 2027 (some articles earlier). The AI Act (EU) 2024/1689 lists machinery among product legislation where AI systems can be high-risk. This is a legal summary from the official texts, not legal advice.
props.Key players: European Commission; notified bodies; national market-surveillance authorities
props.Best resources: EUR-Lex text of Regulation 2023/1230 ; EUR-Lex text of Regulation 2024/1689

aliases: Robotics regulation & compliance in the EU

props.What it is: Learned policies can do unexpected things. A safety filter sits between the policy and the motors and minimally changes unsafe commands; control barrier functions (CBFs) are a common mathematical tool. Safe RL adds constraints during learning.
props.Prerequisites: Control basics; RL basics
props.Frontier state 2026: A 2021 review unifies learning-based control and safe RL; safe-control-gym provides PyBullet benchmarks with symbolic constraints and disturbances (MIT license). 2026 papers add multi-link safety filtering for VLA policies around moving hazards and safety-constrained MPC.
props.Key players: University of Toronto / TUM Learning Systems lab (safe-control-gym); Caltech and others (CBF theory)

knowledge.name: Semantic safety & guardrails for LLM/VLA-controlled robots

props.What it is: When a language or vision-language model controls a robot, safety is also about meaning: refusing a harmful instruction, or noticing that a hot pan should not be handed to a child. Guardrails check plans against safety rules, and benchmarks test whether models judge situations safely.
props.Prerequisites: LLM prompting and APIs; basic robot task planning
props.Frontier state 2026: RoboPAIR (ICRA 2025) jailbroke LLM-controlled robots including a Unitree Go2, often with 100% attack success. RoboGuard (2025) proposes a two-stage guardrail. Google DeepMind released the ASIMOV benchmark (CoRL 2025) for semantic safety of robot foundation models. 2026 papers propose modular guardrails and diagnostic VLA safety benchmarks.
props.Key players: University of Pennsylvania (RoboPAIR, RoboGuard); Google DeepMind (ASIMOV, Gemini Robotics)
props.Best resources: ASIMOV benchmark page ; RoboPAIR page ; arXiv 2503.07885 (RoboGuard)
props.Sources:
https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13691
https://robopair.org/
https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07885
https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08663
https://asimov-benchmark.github.io/v1/
https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04056
https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27079

aliases: Semantic safety & guardrails for LLM/VLA-controlled robots

props.What it is: Instead of only learning from demonstrations collected beforehand, the robot learns while acting: a human corrects it, takes over, or ranks behaviours. Interactive imitation learning and RL from human feedback reduce the gap between what was shown and what the robot actually does.
props.Prerequisites: Imitation learning basics; teleoperation
props.Frontier state 2026: A 2022 survey structures interactive imitation learning; a 2025 survey covers it for dexterous humanoid manipulation; 2026 work includes blended shared control for interactive IL and a scoping review of RLHF for human-robot collaboration.
props.Key players: TU Delft and co-authors (IIL survey); robot-learning labs

knowledge.name: Safety of humanoids & dynamically stable mobile robots

props.What it is: A walking robot cannot simply be switched off when something goes wrong: cutting power makes it fall, which is itself a hazard. Safety for humanoids and self-balancing robots therefore needs new standards and controlled stopping behaviours.
props.Prerequisites: Robot safety standards & risk assessment; locomotion basics
props.Frontier state 2026: ISO/CD 25785-1 (safety requirements for dynamically stable industrial mobile robots, legged or wheeled) is under development. A 2026 paper names the fail-passive gap and pinpoints the robot-side reaction chain as the part not yet certifiable. Unitree G1 is listed from US $13.5K.
props.Key players: ISO TC 299 working groups (not verified in detail); humanoid makers such as Unitree
props.Best resources: ISO search result for 25785 ; arXiv 2608.02809 ; arXiv 2511.23300

aliases: Safety of humanoids & dynamically stable mobile robots

props.What it is: A robot is a set of rigid parts, and every part gets its own coordinate frame. Rotation matrices, quaternions and 4x4 homogeneous transforms convert a point from one frame to another. Almost every robotics bug starts with a wrong frame or a wrong rotation convention.
props.Prerequisites: Linear algebra (matrices, vectors); basic Python/NumPy
props.Frontier state 2026: Mature textbook material. The modern teaching standard (Modern Robotics) uses Lie groups SO(3)/SE(3) and twists. Tooling (Robotics Toolbox for Python, Pinocchio) makes transforms one-liners.
props.Key players: Northwestern (Lynch), SNU (Park), Stanford (Khatib), QUT (Corke)

props.What it is: A robot description file lists the links (with masses, inertias and meshes) and joints (type, axis, limits) of a robot. URDF is the ROS standard and MJCF is MuJoCo's format. Simulators, IK solvers and dynamics libraries all read these files, so a wrong file breaks everything downstream.
props.Prerequisites: Coordinate frames; XML; basic CAD helps
props.Frontier state 2026: Curated model libraries (MuJoCo Menagerie) ship ready-made arms, quadrupeds and humanoids; CAD-to-robot exporters (onshape-to-robot) produce URDF/SDF/MJCF directly from Onshape assemblies, including kinematic loops.
props.Key players: Google DeepMind (MuJoCo, Menagerie), Rhoban/Bordeaux (onshape-to-robot), ROS community

props.What it is: Forward kinematics computes where the robot's hand (end-effector) is, given all joint angles. It chains one transform per joint. The two classic recipes are Denavit-Hartenberg parameters and the product-of-exponentials formula.
props.Prerequisites: Rigid-body motion & coordinate frames
props.Frontier state 2026: Solved for serial arms; still the first building block for every controller, IK solver and learned policy that outputs end-effector poses.
props.Key players: Modern Robotics authors; Springer Handbook ch. 2 (Waldron & Schmiedeler); Stanford CS223A

props.What it is: The Jacobian is a matrix that maps joint speeds to the hand's linear and angular speed, and joint torques to hand forces. At a singularity the Jacobian loses rank: the arm cannot move in some direction no matter how fast the joints spin. Manipulability measures how close the arm is to that.
props.Prerequisites: Forward kinematics; derivatives; matrix rank
props.Frontier state 2026: Standard theory; current tools compute Jacobians, Hessians and manipulability automatically, and differential-IK libraries use them in real time.
props.Key players: Stanford CS223A (Khatib), Modern Robotics, QUT Robotics Toolbox

props.What it is: Inverse kinematics (IK) answers the reverse question: which joint angles put the hand at a target pose? Simple arms have closed-form formulas; general arms need iterative numerical solvers that respect joint limits. There can be zero, one or many solutions.
props.Prerequisites: Forward kinematics; Jacobians; basic optimization
props.Frontier state 2026: Numerical IK is commodity (TRAC-IK combines Newton and SQP solvers to handle joint limits). The open part is speed and robustness for many-DoF robots and many simultaneous goals.
props.Key players: TRACLabs (TRAC-IK), MoveIt community, Modern Robotics

props.What it is: Instead of solving IK once, differential IK computes at every control step a small joint velocity that moves the robot toward several goals at once (hand pose, posture, center of mass) while respecting limits. It is written as a small quadratic program. Robots with more joints than needed (redundant) use the extra freedom for secondary goals.
props.Prerequisites: Jacobians; least squares; quadratic programs (conceptually)
props.Frontier state 2026: Task-based QP IK is now the default for teleoperation, humanoid retargeting and whole-body motion. mink handles floating bases and collision limits; Pink does the same on Pinocchio models.
props.Key players: Kevin Zakka (mink), Stéphane Caron (Pink), Inria/LAAS (Pinocchio)

props.What it is: Wheeled robots cannot slide sideways, which is a 'nonholonomic' constraint. Differential-drive, unicycle and car-like robots share one simple model that turns wheel speeds into forward speed and turning rate. Integrating this model from wheel encoders gives odometry.
props.Prerequisites: Coordinate frames; basic calculus
props.Frontier state 2026: Mature; used everywhere in AMRs and mobile manipulators. Remaining difficulty is wheel slip, which kinematics alone does not model.
props.Key players: Modern Robotics ch. 13, Caltech, ROS navigation community

props.What it is: In a parallel robot (e.g. a delta robot), several legs connect the base to the moving platform, forming closed loops. For these, inverse kinematics is often easy and forward kinematics is hard, the reverse of serial arms. Closed loops also appear inside legs and grippers (linkages).
props.Prerequisites: Forward & inverse kinematics; constraints
props.Frontier state 2026: Closed-loop support is now native in dynamics libraries (Pinocchio) and CAD exporters (onshape-to-robot closing constraints). Accurate simulation of many coupled loops with contacts is still an active topic.
props.Key players: Pinocchio team (Inria), simulation researchers; open-source delta builders

props.What it is: Dynamics links motion to forces: the mass matrix M(q), Coriolis/centrifugal terms and gravity give tau = M(q)q'' + C(q,q')q' + g(q). Inverse dynamics computes the torques needed for a desired motion; forward dynamics computes the motion produced by given torques. This is what physics simulators integrate every step.
props.Prerequisites: Kinematics; Newton's laws; ODEs
props.Frontier state 2026: Classical theory (Lagrange, Newton-Euler, Featherstone's spatial algebra). Taught in MIT Underactuated and Stanford CS223A; underlies all model-based control and simulation.
props.Key players: Roy Featherstone, David Orin (Springer Handbook ch. 3), MIT (Tedrake), Stanford (Khatib)

props.What it is: Recursive algorithms (RNEA for inverse dynamics, ABA for forward dynamics) compute dynamics in time linear in the number of joints. Modern libraries also compute their exact derivatives, which gradient-based optimizers and MPC need.
props.Prerequisites: Rigid-body dynamics; C++/Python
props.Frontier state 2026: Pinocchio (Inria Paris, BSD) provides analytical derivatives of RNEA/ABA, centroidal dynamics, closed loops and frictional contact solvers; it powers Crocoddyl and many humanoid MPC stacks.
props.Key players: Inria Willow / LAAS-CNRS (Carpentier, Mansard), Featherstone

props.What it is: A path says where to go; a trajectory also says when. Time scaling assigns speeds along a path so velocity, acceleration and jerk limits are respected. Jerk-limited (S-curve) profiles make motion smooth and protect hardware.
props.Prerequisites: Kinematics; basic calculus
props.Frontier state 2026: Real-time jerk-limited generators (Ruckig, <1 ms) and time-optimal path parameterization (TOPP-RA) are mature and used in MoveIt. Active work: combining with collision-aware planners and learned policies' outputs.
props.Key players: Ruckig (Berscheid/Kröger), TOPP-RA (Pham & Pham), MoveIt

props.What it is: Identification estimates the real masses, inertias and friction of a robot from recorded motion and torque/current data, because CAD values are wrong. For cheap servos, the friction and motor model often matter more than link inertias. Good identified models shrink the sim-to-real gap.
props.Prerequisites: Rigid-body dynamics; least squares; logging data from motors
props.Frontier state 2026: Physically consistent identification (SDP constraints) is standard in research (BIRDy benchmark). Rhoban's BAM (2024-26) fits extended friction models for common servos (Dynamixel, eRob and the SO-101's Feetech STS3215) and plugs into MuJoCo/mjlab for RL sim-to-real.
props.Key players: Rhoban (Bordeaux), BIRDy authors, Pinocchio regressors

props.What it is: Real robots differ from their URDF by small errors in link lengths and joint offsets. Kinematic calibration measures the robot in many poses and corrects these parameters; hand-eye calibration finds where the camera is relative to the robot. Both are needed before a camera-guided arm can hit a target.
props.Prerequisites: Forward kinematics; least squares; camera basics
props.Frontier state 2026: Recent work removes markers and external sensors, calibrating arm and RGB-D camera together from learned image correspondences (RA-L 2025).
props.Key players: Industrial metrology vendors (not mapped here), academic calibration groups

props.What it is: Legged robots and humanoids are not bolted to the ground: their base is a free 6-DoF body that moves only through contact forces. Centroidal dynamics summarizes the whole robot by its center of mass and momentum, which makes balance and jumping tractable. Optimal control libraries plan whole-body motions with these models.
props.Prerequisites: Rigid-body dynamics; differential IK; optimization
props.Frontier state 2026: Whole-body trajectory optimization and MPC (Crocoddyl, built on Pinocchio) handle multi-contact plans; in 2025-26 these models are often combined with RL tracking policies on low-cost humanoids such as Unitree G1.
props.Key players: LAAS-CNRS / Heriot-Watt (Edinburgh Centre for Robotics) / Inria Willow (Crocoddyl), Unitree, Berkeley

props.What it is: Contacts (feet, fingers, collisions) make dynamics discontinuous: forces appear suddenly. Simulators approximate contact with solvers or soft penalties. Differentiable simulators also return gradients of the outcome with respect to actions or parameters, for optimization and system identification.
props.Prerequisites: Rigid-body dynamics; autodiff/JAX or PyTorch; GPUs
props.Frontier state 2026: MuJoCo Warp (DeepMind + NVIDIA, Newton project) runs MuJoCo on GPUs; its README says differentiability is not yet available (tracked in issue #500). DiffMJX (2025) shows hard-contact gradients are biased and proposes fixes. Gradient quality through contact is still an open problem.
props.Key players: Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, academic groups (DiffMJX: Paulus, Geist, Martius et al.)

props.What it is: Retargeting converts human motion capture or video into joint trajectories for a robot with different proportions and joint limits. It is solved with IK plus constraints against foot sliding and self-collision. The result is the reference motion that RL tracking policies learn to imitate.
props.Prerequisites: Differential IK; URDF/MJCF; motion-capture formats
props.Frontier state 2026: GMR (2025) shows retargeting quality directly limits policy robustness and supports 15+ humanoids including Unitree G1 and Berkeley Humanoid Lite; BeyondMimic trains dynamic skills (cartwheels, sprints) from retargeted LAFAN1 data.
props.Key players: Stanford (C. Karen Liu), UC Berkeley (Sreenath), Unitree

props.What it is: Static balance keeps the centre of mass over supporting feet. Dynamic balance also depends on momentum and contact forces; a support polygon alone cannot guarantee a moving robot will stay upright.
props.Prerequisites: Forces; torque; centre of mass
props.Frontier state 2026: ZMP and contact feasibility remain useful abstractions but depend on contact and model assumptions. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: MIT Underactuated Robotics

props.What it is: A gait describes when each foot touches the ground and when it swings. Phase offsets and duty factors turn the same legs into walking, trotting or bounding patterns.
props.Prerequisites: Trigonometry; foot trajectories
props.Frontier state 2026: Contact timing and smooth transitions matter as much as a visually plausible repeated animation. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Stanford Robotics Club; Petoi; MIT

props.What it is: Simplified models replace many joints with a mass and a small number of contacts. The linear inverted pendulum approximates walking, while a spring-loaded inverted pendulum models bouncing and running.
props.Prerequisites: Differential equations; numerical integration
props.Frontier state 2026: LIPM and SLIP expose useful structure but omit joint limits, impacts and much full-body dynamics. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: MIT Underactuated Robotics

props.What it is: A central pattern generator is a coupled oscillator that produces rhythmic commands. Feedback can reset its phase when feet touch down, rather than replaying a fixed animation regardless of contact.
props.Prerequisites: Gait phases; oscillator equations
props.Frontier state 2026: Biologically inspired rhythm generation is not by itself a guarantee of balance or terrain robustness. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: EPFL BioRob

props.What it is: A biped repeatedly moves its support from one foot to the other. ZMP preview and capture-point ideas choose body motion and steps that help keep the robot from falling.
props.Prerequisites: Reduced-order models; feedback control; linear algebra
props.Frontier state 2026: Classical walking remains an interpretable baseline; uneven contacts and model errors challenge flat-ground assumptions. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: MIT Underactuated Robotics

knowledge.name: Model predictive control for legged robots

props.What it is: MPC repeatedly predicts a short future and optimizes contact forces or motions. Convex approximations can make this fast when contact timing is already chosen.
props.Prerequisites: Optimization; rigid-body dynamics; contact constraints
props.Frontier state 2026: Convex MPC is not the same as solving arbitrary contact discovery; switched and nonlinear tools support richer models. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: MIT Biomimetics; ETH Robotic Systems Lab

aliases: Model predictive control for legged robots

props.What it is: Whole-body control coordinates joints, body posture and contact forces together. It resolves competing tasks while respecting friction and actuator limits.
props.Prerequisites: Robot Jacobians; inverse dynamics; optimization
props.Frontier state 2026: Task hierarchies and optimal-control solvers trade tracking quality against feasibility and computation. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: LAAS-CNRS; Stack of Tasks; ETH

props.What it is: Reinforcement learning trains a policy by rewarding useful movement in simulation. Domain randomization varies friction, masses and delays so the policy is less tied to one simulated world.
props.Prerequisites: Python; neural networks; gait basics; feedback control
props.Frontier state 2026: legged_gym is a historical Isaac Gym baseline; current Isaac Lab and MuJoCo Playground offer newer workflows. Simulation success alone does not establish hardware transfer. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: ETH; NVIDIA Isaac Lab; Google DeepMind

props.What it is: Leg geometry and transmission choices change reach, force capability and impact behaviour. Proprioceptive actuation uses joint-side feedback to control interaction; this node focuses on mechanical trade-offs, not drive electronics.
props.Prerequisites: Linkage kinematics; torque; basic CAD
props.Frontier state 2026: Low inertia and backdrivability help contact control, but torque, heat and structural margins still constrain a design. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Stanford Robotics Club; MIT Biomimetics

props.What it is: Perceptive walking uses terrain observations to adapt foot placement or body motion. Delayed or missing depth data can make an otherwise capable gait unsafe.
props.Prerequisites: Gaits; feedback; depth images; RL or MPC
props.Frontier state 2026: Parkour and recent predictive perception work connect terrain sensing to low-level control; benchmark terrain and sensor faults rather than claiming universal all-terrain ability. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Extreme Parkour authors; ETH Robotic Systems Lab; STEP and "Watch Your Step" humanoid authors (arXiv 2026)

props.What it is: Recovery turns a fallen configuration into a stable standing pose. It needs contact-aware motions and a safe decision about when normal walking should resume.
props.Prerequisites: Contact dynamics; joint limits; RL basics
props.Frontier state 2026: ANYmal research demonstrated learned recovery, but generalization to arbitrary falls, obstacles and damaged hardware is not established. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: ETH Robotic Systems Lab

props.What it is: Rotors produce thrust and moments that control a flying body. Cascaded rate, attitude and position loops separate fast stabilization from slower movement commands.
props.Prerequisites: Rigid-body rotations; PID; forces and torque
props.Frontier state 2026: PX4 documents controller architecture; this is flight stabilization, not aerial mapping or path planning. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: PX4; Bitcraze

props.What it is: Wheel-legged robots can roll for efficiency and step when terrain demands it. The controller must coordinate rolling constraints, contact forces and transitions between modes.
props.Prerequisites: Wheeled kinematics; legged contact dynamics; MPC or RL
props.Frontier state 2026: Recent hybrid work couples rolling, stepping and body interaction; many papers use platform-specific assets rather than a universal controller. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: OmniQuad authors (arXiv 2610.38502); KYON authors (arXiv 2606.30243); ETH Robotic Systems Lab (OCS2)

props.What it is: Retargeting converts human motion to a robot with different joints and proportions. A tracking policy then learns physically possible whole-body movement rather than directly replaying impossible joint angles.
props.Prerequisites: Robot kinematics; motion data; RL; contact dynamics
props.Frontier state 2026: DeepMimic is foundational; OmniH2O and RSS 2025 ASAP address robot motion tracking and deployment mismatch. Human video does not automatically yield safe robot motions. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: DeepMimic authors (UC Berkeley, UBC); OmniH2O authors; ASAP authors (RSS 2025); UC Berkeley HybridRobotics (BeyondMimic whole_body_tracking)

props.What it is: Agile locomotion includes rapid jumps, dynamic obstacle crossing and fast contact changes. It combines precise timing, perception and control rather than just increasing walking speed.
props.Prerequisites: Perceptive walking; RL; contact dynamics; recovery
props.Frontier state 2026: Extreme Parkour reports impressive bounded course performance; safe extrapolation beyond training obstacles remains an open question. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Extreme Parkour authors; ASAP authors

props.What it is: Loco-manipulation coordinates balance and stepping while the robot interacts with an object. The focus here is how object forces and carried mass affect locomotion, not general grasp perception.
props.Prerequisites: Whole-body control; contact dynamics; stability
props.Frontier state 2026: OmniH2O and recent visual humanoid work connect whole-body skills and interaction, but long-horizon robustness needs careful evaluation. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: OmniH2O authors; recent humanoid research teams

props.What it is: Cross-embodiment learning aims to reuse movement knowledge across bodies with different proportions or joints. A shared policy still needs a representation of each robot and careful testing on unseen bodies.
props.Prerequisites: RL locomotion; robot morphology; motion representations
props.Frontier state 2026: Recent generalist and rapid-adaptation preprints propose broader reuse; transfer across many real bodies remains a research question, not a turnkey low-cost platform. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Generalist humanoid and quadruped adaptation researchers

props.What it is: A gripper is the tool at the end of an arm. Parallel jaws pinch, suction uses a pressure difference, and soft fingers bend around objects.
props.Prerequisites: Basic forces; safe actuator operation
props.Frontier state 2026: Match geometry and material to objects before adding learning; no universal gripper handles every surface. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: MIT manipulation course; industrial gripper designers

props.What it is: Contact forces and friction determine whether an object slips. Form closure blocks motion geometrically; force closure uses frictional contacts to resist disturbances.
props.Prerequisites: Vectors; moments; linear algebra
props.Frontier state 2026: Friction models help explain failures but uncertain surface properties limit predictions on hardware. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Lynch and Park; MIT Robot Locomotion Group

props.What it is: A pick-and-place system finds an object, chooses a grasp, moves the arm, and releases it at a destination. Each stage must use consistent coordinates and recover when a grasp fails.
props.Prerequisites: Coordinate frames; basic inverse kinematics; gripper safety
props.Frontier state 2026: Reliable recovery and repeatable evaluation matter more than a single successful video. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: MIT; MoveIt community

props.What it is: Teleoperation lets a person move an arm through a leader arm or another input device. Recording camera images and joint motion produces examples for imitation learning.
props.Prerequisites: Joint limits; calibration; timestamps; emergency stop
props.Frontier state 2026: The 2026 M3-Tele preprint studies synchronized multimodal demonstration collection and compliant whole-body teleoperation. Dataset quality, synchronized cameras and operator ergonomics constrain useful demonstrations; ALOHA 2 improves collection hardware. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Hugging Face LeRobot; ALOHA 2 team

props.What it is: A grasp detector predicts where a gripper could hold an object from an image or point cloud. A good grasp score does not guarantee the arm can reach it without collisions.
props.Prerequisites: Point clouds; camera calibration; grasp mechanics
props.Frontier state 2026: GraspNet supplies a benchmark and Contact-GraspNet predicts 6D grasps; clutter, sensor gaps and execution remain limitations. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: GraspNet team; NVIDIA Contact-GraspNet

props.What it is: Pose estimation finds an object position and orientation relative to a camera. The robot transforms that estimate into its own coordinates to approach the object.
props.Prerequisites: Rigid transforms; camera intrinsics; RGB-D data
props.Frontier state 2026: FoundationPose supports pose estimation and tracking; symmetry, occlusion and calibration still complicate grasp execution. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: NVIDIA FoundationPose team

props.What it is: Motion generation finds joint movements that avoid the table and other obstacles. It must check the arm links and attached objects, not just the gripper.
props.Prerequisites: Inverse kinematics; collision geometry; coordinate frames
props.Frontier state 2026: MoveIt 2 integrates planning and execution; cuRobo offers GPU-accelerated motion generation, with hardware and model requirements. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: MoveIt maintainers; NVIDIA cuRobo

props.What it is: Compliance makes an arm yield instead of pushing rigidly against an obstacle. Impedance control acts like a virtual spring and damper, useful when inserting a peg or following a surface.
props.Prerequisites: Dynamics; feedback control; force limits; contact mechanics
props.Frontier state 2026: M3-Tele (2026 preprint) explicitly combines contact-force feedback and tactile adaptation. Insertion needs contact-aware feedback and safe limits; a position-only hobby arm is not a torque-controlled research arm. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: MIT; robosuite community

props.What it is: Two arms can hold and manipulate an object together. Their motions must coordinate so they do not collide or pull against each other.
props.Prerequisites: Single-arm manipulation; synchronization; shared frames
props.Frontier state 2026: DECO (ICML 2026) studies bimanual visual, proprioceptive and tactile policy conditioning. ALOHA 2 improves bimanual demonstration hardware; coordinated contact and robustness remain difficult. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ALOHA 2 team; Stanford

props.What it is: A mobile manipulator combines an arm with a moving base. The base must stop in a place from which the arm can safely reach and manipulate an object.
props.Prerequisites: Arm planning; base localization; safety zones
props.Frontier state 2026: M3-Tele (2026 preprint) extends whole-body teleoperation toward compliant contact-rich interaction. Mobile ALOHA demonstrates whole-body imitation; deployment in changing rooms still requires robust perception and recovery. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Stanford Mobile ALOHA team

props.What it is: Tactile sensors measure what happens where a finger touches an object. Camera-based gel sensors turn small surface deformations into images that can reveal contact and slip.
props.Prerequisites: Image processing; contact mechanics; sensor mounting
props.Frontier state 2026: DECO (ICML 2026) reports a tactile adapter for bimanual manipulation; results are task-specific, not universal touch robustness. Touch complements vision during occlusion; calibration, gel wear and generalization across objects remain challenges. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: GelSight; tactile robotics community

props.What it is: Cloth and cables change shape while the robot moves them. Unlike a rigid block, they cannot be described by one position and orientation.
props.Prerequisites: Grasping; image processing; contact; learning basics
props.Frontier state 2026: Cloth Funnels uses dynamic actions to improve cloth configuration; generalizing across materials and folds remains difficult. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Columbia Cloth Funnels team

props.What it is: In-hand manipulation changes an object pose while it stays between several fingers. The controller must repeatedly manage which fingers touch, roll or slide.
props.Prerequisites: Contact mechanics; multi-joint control; reinforcement learning
props.Frontier state 2026: STAR (2026 preprint) explores sparse tactile representations for dexterous vision-tactile-language-action policies. LEAP Hand makes research hardware more accessible; contact-rich sim-to-real transfer and reliable sensing remain bottlenecks. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: CMU LEAP Hand team

props.What it is: An arm can move objects by pushing, sliding or pivoting without holding them. These actions exploit contact with the table or a wall.
props.Prerequisites: Friction; rigid-body dynamics; feedback control
props.Frontier state 2026: Contact mode changes make planning difficult; controlled pushing remains a useful complement to grasping. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: MIT; Lynch and Park

props.What it is: Task planning chooses steps such as opening a drawer before picking an item. Motion planning checks that each step can actually be executed by the arm.
props.Prerequisites: State machines; symbolic search; collision-free arm planning
props.Frontier state 2026: Combining symbolic choices with continuous geometry and recovery remains difficult; language plans need executable checks. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: MIT manipulation course; planning research community

props.What it is: Open-vocabulary systems accept descriptions beyond a fixed list of objects. Affordances describe useful actions, such as pulling a handle, rather than just recognizing its name.
props.Prerequisites: Vision-language models; geometry; manipulation planning
props.Frontier state 2026: VoxPoser builds value maps and ReKep uses relational keypoint constraints; physical grounding and failure detection remain essential. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: VoxPoser team; ReKep team

props.What it is: A vision-language-action model maps camera images and instructions to robot actions. Generalist policies aim to reuse experience across tasks, but still need the right action format and robot calibration.
props.Prerequisites: Imitation learning; datasets; arm interfaces; evaluation
props.Frontier state 2026: STAR (2026 preprint) adds touch to the vision-language-action recipe for dexterous manipulation. OpenVLA, Octo and pi0 demonstrate transferable policies; their published results do not guarantee reliable transfer to a low-cost arm. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: OpenVLA team; Octo team; Physical Intelligence

props.What it is: A motor supplies motion; a joint actuator packages that motor with bearings, transmission and structure. Compare brushed servomotors, steppers and brushless motors by torque-speed behaviour, mass and how they mount, rather than by their command protocol.
props.Prerequisites: Basic forces and units; Electronics fundamentals for robots; Smart servos & serial actuator buses for powered tests.
props.Frontier state 2026: Established design choices, not a winner-takes-all technology. Current integration work combines motor, reducer, bearings and thermal path; this node excludes FOC firmware and serial-bus setup.
props.Key players: MIT robotics teaching; maxon; Open Dynamic Robot Initiative

knowledge.name: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty

props.What it is: Sizing means checking whether an actuator can move the actual load repeatedly, not just once at peak torque. Include gravity, acceleration, gear ratio, reflected rotor inertia and heat during the duty cycle.
props.Prerequisites: Electric actuator architectures: mechanical trade-offs; basic algebra and free-body diagrams; motor datasheet units.
props.Frontier state 2026: Continuous and peak ratings remain different constraints. maxon documents temperature-dependent motor data; real winding temperature and assembly heat transfer must be measured rather than inferred from a catalogue peak.
props.Key players: maxon; MIT Modern Robotics teaching

aliases: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty
