props.What it is: Gears trade speed for torque while changing direction or packaging. A planetary train places smaller planet gears around a sun gear; housing, tooth count, backlash and bearing alignment affect whether it works well.
props.Prerequisites: Electric actuator architectures: mechanical trade-offs; basic ratios; CAD sketches.
props.Frontier state 2026: Planetary and spur gearing are established. Printed teaching models explain reduction but their friction, tooth strength and backlash do not establish industrial actuator performance.
props.Key players: Harmonic Drive planetary products; MIT machine-design teaching

props.What it is: An eccentric input makes a lobed disc move around a ring of pins. An output mechanism removes that wobble to obtain slow rotation; tolerances, bearing loads and disc balancing matter as much as the theoretical ratio.
props.Prerequisites: Spur and planetary gear trains; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints.
props.Frontier state 2026: Nabtesco documents a two-stage RV mechanism. Student printed cycloidal reducers are useful experiments, not drop-in substitutes for precision commercial reducers.
props.Key players: Nabtesco; MIT machine-design teaching

props.What it is: A wave generator flexes a thin toothed cup into an oval so it engages a rigid ring. A small tooth-count difference gives large reduction, but flexspline fatigue, elastic twist and manufacturing accuracy constrain the design.
props.Prerequisites: Spur and planetary gear trains; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; material elasticity.
props.Frontier state 2026: Harmonic Drive explains metal flexspline and wave-generator operation. Vendor zero-backlash claims do not mean infinite stiffness or that a printed educational flexspline has the same rating.
props.Key players: Harmonic Drive; MIT machine-design teaching

props.What it is: Belts and wrapped cables move torque away from the motor, reducing moving mass at a joint. Belt tension, pulley alignment and cable preload set stiffness, slip and usable travel; a capstan is not simply an unlimited-rotation cable pulley.
props.Prerequisites: Spur and planetary gear trains; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; safe handling of tensioned elements.
props.Frontier state 2026: MIT design notes discuss belt tension and capstan termination; ODRI provides pulley-based actuator assembly examples. Low apparent backlash still needs load-reversal and tension-loss testing.
props.Key players: Open Dynamic Robot Initiative; MIT machine-design teaching

knowledge.name: Lead screws, ball screws and linear joint packaging

props.What it is: A rotating screw turns motor motion into linear travel. Lead screws slide while ball screws use rolling balls; lead, guide alignment, buckling, preload and backdriving determine whether a linear joint is suitable.
props.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Bearings, structures and printed load paths.
props.Frontier state 2026: MIT design notes contrast sliding and rolling screws and explain over-constrained guide alignment. Do not assume every screw self-locks; gravity loads need an independent retention assessment.
props.Key players: MIT machine-design teaching; linear-motion component designers

aliases: Lead screws, ball screws and linear joint packaging

knowledge.name: Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design

props.What it is: A linkage constrains several connected pieces to make a useful path; cams shape motion through a profile. Serial, closed-loop and parallel arrangements trade reach, stiffness and assembly complexity, while singular configurations can jam or amplify loads.
props.Prerequisites: Basic geometry and forces; CAD sketches. Full inverse kinematics belongs in Kinematics & dynamics.
props.Frontier state 2026: MIT mechanism teaching grounds joint primitives and open/closed chains. DLR uses shaped cams in variable-stiffness joints; the focus here is geometry and load paths rather than a general motion-planning node.
props.Key players: MIT robotics teaching; DLR

aliases: Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design

knowledge.name: Tendon routing, antagonism and underactuated mechanisms

props.What it is: Tendons pull but do not push, so routing, pretension and a return spring or opposing tendon determine movement. Underactuation uses fewer motors than joints, making the mechanical coupling useful but also harder to predict.
props.Prerequisites: Timing-belt and capstan transmissions; Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design; Grasp mechanics for hand applications.
props.Frontier state 2026: RSS 2025 RUKA and RSS 2024 pneumatic-arm research expose routing and low-distal-mass trade-offs. This node studies transmission and coupling, not another gripper-design or dexterous-policy node.
props.Key players: RUKA authors; DLR; RSS pneumatic-arm authors

aliases: Tendon routing, antagonism and underactuated mechanisms

props.What it is: Backdrivability means an external load can move the actuator backwards. Transparency describes how little extra inertia and friction the mechanism adds; low gear ratio helps but does not by itself prove low friction or safe contact.
props.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Spur and planetary gear trains; guarded test fixtures.
props.Frontier state 2026: Modern Robotics explains squared gear-ratio effects on reflected inertia. MIT Cheetah actuator research grounds low-ratio design; transparency and passive safety must be measured, not inferred from current sensing.
props.Key players: MIT Biomimetic Robotics; Modern Robotics authors

props.What it is: A deliberate spring between drive and output stores energy and makes output force observable through spring deflection. The spring also introduces resonance and limits bandwidth, so stiffness selection and mechanical stops are design decisions.
props.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Backdrivability, friction and mechanical transparency; elementary spring forces.
props.Frontier state 2026: DLR references distinguish intentional series elasticity from incidental gearbox compliance. Elasticity trades shock tolerance and energy storage against deflection and dynamics; it is not a universal improvement.
props.Key players: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics; compliant-actuator researchers

props.What it is: Variable-stiffness hardware changes its physical spring behaviour rather than merely changing a controller gain. Cams, moving lever arms or opposing spring-loaded motors can adjust how strongly a joint resists displacement.
props.Prerequisites: Series-elastic actuator mechanics; Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design; Control fundamentals for powered experiments.
props.Frontier state 2026: DLR David documents antagonism, BAVS and Floating Spring Joint concepts. The research question is useful stiffness range versus mass, energy and complexity, not an unsupported claim of new 2026 adoption.
props.Key players: DLR; authors of the variable-stiffness actuator design review

knowledge.name: Bearings, structures and printed load paths

props.What it is: Bearings guide rotation while the surrounding frame carries loads into the base. Shaft support, fits, fasteners and print orientation matter: a strong motor cannot rescue a flexible bracket or a bearing seat that creeps.
props.Prerequisites: Basic forces, moments and material elasticity; measuring tools; safe fabrication induction.
props.Frontier state 2026: SKF distinguishes bearing families; Prusa explains print-aware modeling. Printed prototypes need measured stiffness and fit checks; catalogue material strength is not a complete printed-part rating.
props.Key players: SKF; Prusa Research; ODRI hardware authors

aliases: Bearings, structures and printed load paths

knowledge.name: CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints

props.What it is: Parametric CAD describes parts using dimensions and constraints so changes remain consistent. Robot design also needs assemblies, tolerance allowances, fastener access, serviceable cable paths and a believable mass model before fabrication.
props.Prerequisites: Basic geometry; introductory mechanical drawing; Bearings, structures and printed load paths for loaded parts.
props.Frontier state 2026: FreeCAD provides parametric modeling and assembly capabilities; onshape-to-robot exports robot descriptions. CAD export is a starting model, not proof of correct inertia, friction or manufacturing tolerances.
props.Key players: FreeCAD contributors; onshape-to-robot maintainers; Prusa Research

aliases: CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints

props.What it is: Pressurized liquid or air drives a piston or contracting muscle. Force depends on pressure and effective area; seals, hoses, compressibility, pumps or compressors and leakage change the complete system, not just the actuator.
props.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; elementary pressure and fluid units; supervised pressure-system safety.
props.Frontier state 2026: RSS 2024 demonstrates a pneumatic-muscle tendon arm. Boston Dynamics retired hydraulic Atlas for an electric successor in 2024; that is one platform decision, not proof that hydraulics are obsolete.
props.Key players: Festo; RSS pneumatic-arm authors; Boston Dynamics

knowledge.name: Soft pneumatic actuators and compliant-body fabrication

props.What it is: An elastomer chamber bends or extends when inflated because its geometry constrains expansion unevenly. Molds, wall thickness, reinforcement and repeatable sealing are the mechanism, rather than a separate rigid gearbox.
props.Prerequisites: Hydraulic and pneumatic transmission mechanics; CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints; materials handling induction.
props.Frontier state 2026: The Harvard-origin Soft Robotics Toolkit documents PneuNets design, fabrication and testing. Reliable pressure-angle behaviour and fatigue remain tasks to measure; do not extrapolate a single bending video into industrial durability.
props.Key players: Harvard Biodesign Lab; Soft Robotics Toolkit contributors

aliases: Soft pneumatic actuators and compliant-body fabrication

knowledge.name: Artificial muscles: electrohydraulic and smart-material actuation

props.What it is: Artificial muscles change shape directly using materials or internal fluids rather than a rotating motor. Electrohydraulic pouches such as HASEL and HALVE combine electrical attraction with fluid displacement; shape-memory and piezoelectric approaches occupy different force, stroke and thermal regimes.
props.Prerequisites: Soft pneumatic actuators and compliant-body fabrication; material mechanics; specialist high-voltage safety before any energized electrohydraulic work.
props.Frontier state 2026: The 2024 HALVE paper reduces voltage relative to prior electrohydraulic actuators, but its reported 1100 V is not hobby-safe low voltage. Other smart-material families are acknowledged here, not claimed comprehensively surveyed or ready for procurement. A 2025 SMA microactuator paper demonstrates thermally controlled folding and magnetic latching; a PNAS origami arm demonstrates magnetic actuation. These are research-specific mechanisms, not interchangeable muscles.
props.Key players: ETH Zurich Soft Robotics Lab; HALVE paper authors

aliases: Artificial muscles: electrohydraulic and smart-material actuation

knowledge.name: Integrated legged and humanoid joint co-design

props.What it is: A useful leg or humanoid joint balances torque, speed, mass, cooling, travel, impact tolerance and maintenance. Quasi-direct drive uses a relatively low reduction ratio with a torque-dense motor; parallel links or remote drives offer other packaging trade-offs.
props.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; Backdrivability, friction and mechanical transparency; BLDC motor control & field-oriented control (FOC) for powered drives.
props.Frontier state 2026: ODRI exposes module assembly and test stands; ToddlerBot documents maintainable hardware and 2025/2026 releases. Atlas 2026 manufacturer statements give ecosystem context, not public internal actuator specs or independently verified deployment performance.
props.Key players: Open Dynamic Robot Initiative; Stanford ToddlerBot team; MIT Biomimetic Robotics; Boston Dynamics

aliases: Integrated legged and humanoid joint co-design

props.What it is: A camera turns 3D points into 2D pixels through a lens. The pinhole model, focal length, principal point and lens distortion describe this mapping, so code can go from pixels back to rays in the world.
props.Prerequisites: Linear algebra (matrices, homogeneous coordinates); Python/NumPy
props.Frontier state 2026: Mature theory; still the base of every 3D perception pipeline. Learned models (VGGT, Depth Anything 3) now also predict camera parameters from images. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Textbook authors (Szeliski; Hartley & Zisserman; Corke); OpenCV community

props.What it is: Calibration measures a camera's internal parameters and where it sits relative to the robot. You show a checkerboard or ChArUco board from many angles and solve for the parameters; hand-eye calibration links camera frame and gripper frame.
props.Prerequisites: Camera models; rigid transforms
props.Frontier state 2026: Standard tooling exists (OpenCV, ROS camera_calibration, Kalibr for camera-IMU). Low-cost arm demos such as Google's SO-101 pointing sample still rely on a ChArUco homography step. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ETH Zurich ASL (Kalibr); OpenCV; ROS image_pipeline maintainers

props.What it is: Before deep learning, robots found edges, corners, colors and keypoints with hand-written filters. Matching keypoints between images gives motion and 3D structure, and simple color thresholds are still the fastest way to get a first demo.
props.Prerequisites: Python; arrays; basic linear algebra
props.Frontier state 2026: Still used for fast, explainable baselines and in SLAM front-ends; learned matchers compete for hard cases. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: OpenCV; university perception courses (UMD ENPM673)

props.What it is: Fiducials are printed black-and-white square codes that software detects reliably and uses to compute the 6D pose of the tag. They are the quickest way to give a robot accurate object or camera positions without training a model.
props.Prerequisites: Camera calibration
props.Frontier state 2026: Mature and widely used for ground truth, calibration and docking; AprilTag 3 library is the open reference. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: University of Michigan APRIL Lab; OpenCV ArUco module

props.What it is: Depth cameras give a distance for each pixel. Stereo cameras compare two views (triangulation), active cameras add a projected IR pattern or time-of-flight light. Knowing their noise and failure cases (shiny, transparent, dark surfaces) is essential.
props.Prerequisites: Camera models; calibration
props.Frontier state 2026: Commodity RGB-D cameras (OAK-D, ZED, RealSense) are standard; learned stereo such as FoundationStereo (2025) claims strong zero-shot matching. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Luxonis; Stereolabs; RealSense SDK; NVIDIA (FoundationStereo)

props.What it is: A point cloud is a list of 3D points from a depth camera or LiDAR. Typical steps are downsampling, removing outliers, finding the table plane, clustering objects and aligning two clouds (ICP registration).
props.Prerequisites: Stereo & RGB-D depth sensing; rigid transforms
props.Frontier state 2026: Open3D and PCL are the standard libraries; learned 3D networks sit on top of the same preprocessing. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Open3D developers; PCL community

props.What it is: A detector draws boxes and class labels around objects in each image. Models such as YOLO run in real time on a laptop GPU or edge board and can be fine-tuned on a few hundred labeled images of your own objects.
props.Prerequisites: Python; basic deep learning (PyTorch)
props.Frontier state 2026: Ultralytics ships YOLO11 (2024) and YOLO26, with YOLO27 announced as 'coming soon' on its docs; RT-DETR offers a transformer alternative. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Ultralytics; Stanford CS231n (teaching)

props.What it is: Segmentation labels the exact pixels of each object, not just a box. Meta's Segment Anything models cut out any object from a click, box or (SAM 3) a short text phrase, and track masks through video.
props.Prerequisites: Real-time 2D object detection basics; PyTorch
props.Frontier state 2026: SAM 2 (2024) added video memory; SAM 3 (Nov 2025, ICLR 2026) adds promptable concept segmentation from noun phrases or exemplars and is open-sourced. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Meta (FAIR / Meta Superintelligence Labs); IDEA Research (Grounded-SAM-2)

props.What it is: Tracking keeps the same ID on each object across frames, so a robot knows 'this is still the same cup'. Most trackers link detector boxes over time with motion prediction (Kalman filter) and matching.
props.Prerequisites: Real-time 2D object detection; basic probability
props.Frontier state 2026: Tracking-by-detection (ByteTrack, BoxMOT collection) remains the practical default; SAM 2/3 offer mask-level tracking. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ByteTrack authors; BoxMOT maintainers; Ultralytics tracking mode

props.What it is: A neural network guesses depth from a single ordinary image. Recent models output metric depth (in meters) good enough for rough obstacle maps and for replacing a depth camera in cheap setups, though not for precise grasping.
props.Prerequisites: Camera models; deep learning basics
props.Frontier state 2026: Depth Anything V2 (2024), Apple Depth Pro (2024, metric) and Depth Anything 3 (Nov 2025, any-view geometry) are open; FetchBot (CoRL 2025) uses predicted depth for sim-to-real. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ByteDance Seed / HKU (Depth Anything); Apple ML Research (Depth Pro)

props.What it is: Pose trackers find body joints or the 21 keypoints of a hand in video. Robots use them for gesture commands, safety zones and to retarget human hand motion into robot teleoperation or demonstrations.
props.Prerequisites: Real-time 2D object detection; coordinate frames
props.Frontier state 2026: Google MediaPipe Hand/Pose Landmarker run in real time on CPU/phone; industrial cobot surveys list gesture recognition and safety monitoring as core perception tasks. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Google AI Edge (MediaPipe); Ultralytics pose models

props.What it is: LiDAR measures distance with laser pulses and gives a precise 3D point cloud around the robot. 3D detectors find cars, people or boxes as 3D boxes in these clouds, as in autonomous driving datasets like KITTI.
props.Prerequisites: Point cloud processing; deep learning
props.Frontier state 2026: OpenPCDet is a common open toolbox; low-cost hybrid-solid LiDARs (Livox Mid-360) target mobile robots. Multi-sensor fusion is an active embodied-AI research area. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Livox; OpenMMLab (OpenPCDet); KITTI (KIT/Toyota TI)

props.What it is: Open-vocabulary detectors find objects from any text you type ('the red mug'), without retraining on fixed classes. They link language models and vision so a robot can be told what to look for.
props.Prerequisites: Real-time 2D object detection; transformers basics
props.Frontier state 2026: Grounding DINO (2023), OWLv2 (2023), Florence-2 and SAM 3 concept prompts are open; Grounded-SAM-2 chains detection, segmentation and tracking. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: IDEA Research; Google (OWL-ViT/OWLv2); Microsoft (Florence-2); Meta (SAM 3)

props.What it is: Foundation vision backbones are networks pretrained on huge image sets without labels. Their features describe image patches so well that a small head can do depth, segmentation or correspondence, and many robot policies use them as their 'eyes'.
props.Prerequisites: Deep learning; transformers
props.Frontier state 2026: DINOv2 (2023) is widely reused; Depth Anything 3 uses a plain DINO encoder as backbone. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Meta FAIR

props.What it is: Point trackers follow any chosen pixel through a video, even through occlusion. Robotics uses them to turn human or robot videos into motion data and to measure how objects move.
props.Prerequisites: Deep learning; video basics
props.Frontier state 2026: CoTracker3 (Meta, 2024) and TAPIR (DeepMind) are open; used to extract motion from videos for robot learning. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Meta (CoTracker); Google DeepMind (TAPIR/TAPNet)

props.What it is: New transformer models take a few ordinary photos and directly output 3D points and camera poses in one pass, replacing slow classical photogrammetry. This gives robots quick 3D models of scenes from cheap cameras.
props.Prerequisites: Camera models; deep learning
props.Frontier state 2026: DUSt3R (2023), VGGT (2025, CVPR 2025 Best Paper Award) and Depth Anything 3 (2025, reports +35.7% camera-pose accuracy over VGGT on its benchmark). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: NAVER LABS Europe (DUSt3R, Grenoble); Oxford VGG & Meta (VGGT); ByteDance Seed (DA3)

props.What it is: NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting build photo-realistic, viewable 3D scenes from many photos. Robotics uses them for digital twins, simulation assets and maps that can be rendered from new viewpoints.
props.Prerequisites: Camera models; calibration; GPU programming basics helpful
props.Frontier state 2026: 3DGS (Inria, 2023) became standard; nerfstudio and gsplat are open toolkits; 2025-2026 work extends splats to SLAM, event cameras and articulated objects (ScrewSplat, CoRL 2025). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Inria GRAPHDECO; nerfstudio (UC Berkeley); research labs

props.What it is: A 3D scene graph stores the objects in a room, where they are and how they relate ('cup on table'), with language labels from foundation models. Robots query it with text to find and fetch things.
props.Prerequisites: Open-vocabulary detection; point clouds; RGB-D sensing
props.Frontier state 2026: ConceptGraphs (2023) and OK-Robot (2024) show open-knowledge pick-and-drop in homes; surveys (2025) frame 3D foundation models as possible unified representation. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ConceptGraphs team (MIT, Montreal, Toronto); NYU (OK-Robot)

props.What it is: Large vision-language models answer questions about images, point to objects and estimate progress, acting as a high-level 'brain' for a robot. They turn a camera image plus a sentence into coordinates or plans.
props.Prerequisites: Open-vocabulary detection; calibration (pixel-to-robot mapping)
props.Frontier state 2026: Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5 (Sept 2025) is marketed for pointing, detection and success detection via API; Google publishes an SO-101 pointing sample. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Google DeepMind; open VLM community

props.What it is: Event cameras report per-pixel brightness changes asynchronously with microsecond latency instead of full frames. They handle fast motion and extreme lighting where normal cameras blur, but need new algorithms.
props.Prerequisites: Camera models; signal processing basics
props.Frontier state 2026: Active research (event SLAM survey in IJCV 2026, event-based Gaussian splatting); Prophesee (Paris) ships sensors and the Metavision SDK. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Prophesee (Paris); UZH Robotics & Perception Group

props.What it is: A configuration is the set of numbers describing a robot pose, such as joint angles or vehicle position. Collision checking rejects configurations and connecting motions that intersect obstacles; a free endpoint alone is not enough.
props.Prerequisites: Coordinate frames; basic geometry. Arm-specific integration belongs to Manipulation: Collision-free arm motion generation.
props.Frontier state 2026: Geometry, distance queries and conservative motion validation remain essential even when a neural network proposes the path. Collision discretization can miss thin obstacles. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Kavraki Lab / OMPL contributors; MoveIt community / PickNik Robotics

props.What it is: Dijkstra searches a graph for a cheapest route; A* uses a lower-bound distance estimate to focus that search. D* Lite reuses earlier search work when edge costs change, useful when a robot discovers a blocked passage.
props.Prerequisites: Graphs; priority queues; Configuration space & collision checking.
props.Frontier state 2026: A heuristic must satisfy the algorithm assumptions for optimality claims. A shortest route on a coarse grid is not necessarily a shortest executable robot trajectory. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Open Navigation / ROS navigation community

props.What it is: PRM builds a network of sampled safe states; RRT grows a tree toward random samples. RRT* improves solution quality with more samples, but finite computation does not promise the best path.
props.Prerequisites: Configuration space & collision checking; probability; graph search. Reuse Manipulation: Collision-free arm motion generation for arm execution, not a second arm pipeline.
props.Frontier state 2026: OMPL provides abstract state-space planners for vehicles, drones and manipulators, not a complete collision checker or visualizer. Benchmark multiple seeds and time budgets, including narrow passages. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Kavraki Lab / OMPL contributors

props.What it is: A path says where to go; a trajectory also says when. Time parameterization assigns speed along a path while respecting limits, while online trajectory generation can react to new target states.
props.Prerequisites: Paths; derivatives; velocity and acceleration limits; basic Control concepts.
props.Frontier state 2026: Ruckig handles jerk-limited state-to-state trajectory generation; TOPPRA time-parameterizes given paths. Retiming or smoothing must be followed by constraint and collision checks; they are not interchangeable methods. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Lars Berscheid / Ruckig contributors; Hung Pham and TOPPRA contributors

props.What it is: Trajectory optimization adjusts a sequence of states or actions to reduce costs such as roughness, travel time and proximity to obstacles. CHOMP and TrajOpt are examples; an MPC-style planner repeats optimization after each new observation.
props.Prerequisites: Calculus; numerical optimization; trajectory constraints. Manipulation: Collision-free arm motion generation covers the arm-specific application.
props.Frontier state 2026: Local optimizers can get stuck and penalty costs are not proof of safety. Compare initializations, feasible baselines and explicit constraint violations rather than attractive videos alone. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: MoveIt community / PickNik Robotics

props.What it is: A navigation stack joins map handling, route planning, path following and recovery behaviors. A costmap turns sensor and map information into traversal costs, including the space a robot body needs around obstacles.
props.Prerequisites: Graph search & incremental replanning; ROS 2; supplied localization and transforms (SLAM itself is outside this branch).
props.Frontier state 2026: Nav2 separates planners, controllers and behaviors into servers and plugins. Treat unknown space, stale observations and footprint inflation explicitly; navigation software is not a certified safety system. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Open Navigation / ROS navigation community

props.What it is: Local planners choose the next short motion using nearby obstacles and a longer route. DWA samples admissible velocities, MPPI samples action rollouts, and TEB optimizes a timed band; these are different tradeoffs, not universal replacements.
props.Prerequisites: Navigation stacks & costmaps; vehicle motion models; basic feedback control.
props.Frontier state 2026: MPPI parallel rollout optimization is well established; controller tuning still depends on dynamics, horizon and sensor delay. A short horizon can prefer a dead end, and moving people require conservative testing. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Open Navigation / ROS navigation community

props.What it is: A behavior tree connects small actions and conditions into a reactive program. Unlike a planner that invents a sequence, an executive runs and interrupts actions, checks results and chooses recovery branches.
props.Prerequisites: Async programming; finite-state machines; ROS actions for integration. For manipulation task-and-motion coupling, see Long-horizon / task-and-motion planning.
props.Frontier state 2026: BehaviorTree.CPP provides asynchronous actions, XML trees and logging; Nav2 uses trees to orchestrate servers. Correct cancellation, timeout and failure propagation matter more than tree size. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Open Navigation / ROS navigation community; Davide Faconti / BehaviorTree.CPP contributors

props.What it is: PDDL describes actions using conditions that must hold and effects that change the world. A symbolic planner finds an action sequence, but it cannot guarantee geometric feasibility unless another component checks it.
props.Prerequisites: Logic; search; Behavior trees & task executives. Cross-reference Manipulation: Long-horizon / task-and-motion planning for joint symbolic/geometric manipulation.
props.Frontier state 2026: PlanSys2 provides a ROS 2 PDDL planning framework. Model missing facts and failed effects explicitly; do not mistake a valid symbolic plan for successful physical execution. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Francisco Martin and PlanSys2 contributors

props.What it is: A car cannot slide sideways, and a flying robot cannot change velocity instantly. Kinodynamic planning searches motions that obey dynamics; lattices and Hybrid A* account for heading and permitted motion primitives for vehicles.
props.Prerequisites: Sampling-based motion planning; differential equations; vehicle models; trajectory limits.
props.Frontier state 2026: Choose a model and steering or propagation method that matches the platform. Car-like search and drone dynamics are not interchangeable; a collision-free geometric curve may still be impossible to fly or drive. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Kavraki Lab / OMPL contributors; Open Navigation / ROS navigation community

props.What it is: Multi-agent path finding assigns time-aware routes so robots do not collide or swap through each other. Conflict-based search resolves conflicts between individual routes; task allocation and physical tracking are separate problems.
props.Prerequisites: Graph search & incremental replanning; discrete time; collision definitions.
props.Frontier state 2026: Grid MAPF makes strong assumptions about timing and robot size. Delays and continuous footprints need additional checking, so an optimal discrete schedule is not proof of safe fleet execution. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: atb033 repository contributors

props.What it is: Coverage plans visit an entire region rather than just reaching one goal. Sweep patterns and cell decomposition help inspection, cleaning and agriculture account for tool width, overlaps and obstacles.
props.Prerequisites: Geometry; graph search; robot turning constraints.
props.Frontier state 2026: Fields2Cover implements agricultural coverage building blocks. Coverage percentage must include inaccessible areas and turning feasibility; a pretty sweep plot alone does not prove all reachable space was serviced. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Fields2Cover contributors

props.What it is: An MDP chooses actions with uncertain outcomes; a POMDP also handles uncertainty about the current state. A belief is a distribution over possible states, allowing actions that gather information before committing to a route.
props.Prerequisites: Probability; Bayes rule; value iteration; graph search. State estimation is a prerequisite, not remapped here.
props.Frontier state 2026: POMDPs.jl separates models and solvers. A 2026 semantic-uncertainty planning preprint connects task specifications and kinodynamic search; guarantees depend on its stated model assumptions and do not cover arbitrary perception errors. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: JuliaPOMDP contributors

props.What it is: Many candidate motions can be checked or optimized simultaneously on a GPU. This accelerates planning components rather than removing geometry, dynamics or safety constraints.
props.Prerequisites: Sampling-based motion planning; Optimization-based trajectory planning; CUDA-capable computing. Arm applications stay in Manipulation: Collision-free arm motion generation.
props.Frontier state 2026: The cuRobo site reports 2026 whole-body and GPU planning updates, beyond its original arm-focused release. Treat vendor timing claims as setup-specific and measure synchronization, memory and collision fidelity on available hardware. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Kavraki Lab / OMPL contributors; NVIDIA

props.What it is: A learned planner predicts useful paths, samples or costs from training examples. Diffusion planners generate several possible trajectories by iterative denoising, but predictions still need validity checks and fallback planning.
props.Prerequisites: Sampling-based motion planning; neural networks; train/test splits; collision validation.
props.Frontier state 2026: Cascaded Diffusion Models for Neural Motion Planning (2025) combines coarse and fine prediction with online repair across navigation and manipulation domains. This is a bounded paper result, not a general safety guarantee or proof of unseen-environment reliability. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Kavraki Lab / OMPL contributors; Mohit Sharma; Adam Fishman; Vikash Kumar; Chris Paxton; Oliver Kroemer

props.What it is: A language model can propose skills or translate instructions into a formal planning problem. Grounding checks whether the robot actually has the skills and whether preconditions and observed results match the plan.
props.Prerequisites: Symbolic task planning with PDDL; Behavior trees & task executives. Manipulation-specific integration remains in Long-horizon / task-and-motion planning, not duplicated here.
props.Frontier state 2026: SayCan grounds skill selection in affordance scores; Code as Policies generates programs; LLM+P delegates formal search to a planner. EmboTeam (2026 preprint) adds monitored multi-robot grounding; none licenses unguarded model-generated robot commands. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Davide Faconti / BehaviorTree.CPP contributors; Francisco Martin and PlanSys2 contributors; Google Research / Everyday Robots research team

props.What it is: A world model predicts the result of candidate actions, letting a planner imagine alternatives before executing a short prefix. This differs from simply replaying a learned policy: the planner evaluates predicted futures at decision time.
props.Prerequisites: Planning under uncertainty & belief space; neural networks; MPC; dataset coverage.
props.Frontier state 2026: DINO-WM (2024) plans over pretrained visual features; LaDi-WM (CoRL 2025) couples predicted latent states to policies. A 2026 preprint explores RRT/KPIECE with world-model propagation; model errors can be exploited by search, so validate closed-loop outcomes. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: DINO-WM paper authors

knowledge.name: Robot learning problem formulation: observations, actions, policies

props.What it is: A policy is a function that turns sensor observations into robot commands. Choosing what the robot observes, what an action means, and how often it acts is part of the learning problem, not just an implementation detail.
props.Prerequisites: Python arrays; basic probability; robot joint and coordinate-frame vocabulary
props.Frontier state 2026: Observation histories help with hidden state; action units and control frequency must agree between data and deployment. Start with a small explicit interface before trying a generalist policy. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: MIT manipulation course; ARISE Initiative

aliases: Robot learning problem formulation: observations, actions, policies

props.What it is: A robot-learning toolchain stores episodes, trains policies, and replays their results. Formats such as LeRobotDataset and RLDS record observations and actions with timing and episode boundaries so different programs can use the same experience.
props.Prerequisites: Python; tables; video files; episode and timestep concepts
props.Frontier state 2026: LeRobotDataset v3 documents scalable storage; RLDS provides episodic interchange but its repository is archived. Conversions must preserve timestamps, action conventions, terminal flags and data licenses rather than just rename columns. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Hugging Face LeRobot; Google Research; ARISE Initiative

props.What it is: Evaluation asks whether a policy completes a task on trials it did not train on. A useful test fixes success rules and reset conditions, counts failures, and separates familiar scenes from new objects, backgrounds or tasks.
props.Prerequisites: Basic statistics; train/test splits; safe experiment resets
props.Frontier state 2026: LIBERO and RoboCasa expose structured generalization tests, not a universal real-world score. Hold out episodes and environments, report uncertainty across seeds, and distinguish simulated success from physical reliability. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: LIBERO authors; RoboCasa authors; ARISE Initiative

props.What it is: These policies generate a sequence of robot commands by gradually transforming noise into actions. Unlike averaging all demonstrations into one answer, a generative policy can represent several valid ways to solve the same scene.
props.Prerequisites: Imitation learning (behavior cloning); neural networks; conditional probability
props.Frontier state 2026: Diffusion Policy is a strong specialist reference; pi0 uses flow matching for general robot control. Denoising steps, action horizon and inference delay must be evaluated together; published success does not imply SO-101 compatibility. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Columbia; Stanford; Physical Intelligence

props.What it is: Action chunking predicts several future commands at once instead of one command at each camera frame. Tokenization converts continuous commands into symbols; FAST compresses an action sequence in frequency space rather than binning every value independently.
props.Prerequisites: Imitation learning (behavior cloning); time-series arrays; transformer basics
props.Frontier state 2026: ACT motivates chunked prediction and temporal ensembling; FAST addresses high-frequency action tokenization. Compression error, chunk length and feedback delay are different trade-offs and should be measured separately. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Stanford ACT authors; Physical Intelligence FAST authors

props.What it is: A visual encoder turns camera images into feature vectors before a small policy chooses actions. Reusing an encoder trained on large image or video collections can reduce training work, but features that recognize objects may still miss details needed for precise control.
props.Prerequisites: Image tensors; neural network embeddings; supervised learning
props.Frontier state 2026: R3M, VC-1 and DINOv2 are complementary reference encoders rather than a 2026 ranking. CortexBench finds no universally dominant representation; frozen-feature and fine-tuned comparisons need matched data and control heads. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: R3M authors; Meta FAIR; CortexBench collaboration

props.What it is: Offline reinforcement learning improves a policy using a fixed collection of past transitions and rewards, without exploring during training. Its main trap is trusting actions that look valuable to the model but are poorly covered by the recorded data.
props.Prerequisites: Reinforcement learning for robots; value functions; reward definitions
props.Frontier state 2026: CQL penalizes optimistic out-of-data values and IQL avoids evaluating unseen actions during value learning. Implementation and dataset changes can alter conclusions; use behavior cloning and matched splits as baselines before online transfer. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: UC Berkeley; CQL and IQL authors

props.What it is: A reward tells a learning system which outcomes are desirable, but a convenient score may not match the real goal. Reward learning uses examples or feedback to estimate that score, while language and vision models can help propose or judge rewards.
props.Prerequisites: Reinforcement learning for robots; validation labels; false positives
props.Frontier state 2026: Eureka generates reward code; D&A (2026 preprint) separates video description from progress assessment to address VLM reward bias. Neither makes an unsupervised success judge trustworthy by default; test failed and ambiguous episodes independently. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: NVIDIA Eureka authors; D&A authors

props.What it is: A policy can drift into situations missing from its demonstrations. Interactive imitation asks a person for correct actions in those visited states, then adds the corrections to training instead of repeatedly collecting only perfect expert runs.
props.Prerequisites: Imitation learning (behavior cloning); safe override interface; dataset versioning
props.Frontier state 2026: DAgger explains distribution shift and iterative expert labeling. Robotic Data Inoculation (2026 preprint) explores human correction under learned perturbations; treat it as research, not permission for unsafe online exploration. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: DAgger authors; UC Berkeley Data Inoculation authors

props.What it is: Augmentation changes training examples while keeping their intended action or outcome valid. Synthetic demonstration generation goes further by adapting trajectories to new scenes, so a few human demonstrations can cover more starting conditions.
props.Prerequisites: Imitation learning (behavior cloning); coordinate transforms; simulator resets
props.Frontier state 2026: MimicGen adapts object-relative trajectory segments; Augmentron (2026 preprint) targets temporal and multi-camera visual consistency. Synthetic volume is not equivalent to independent coverage: track failed generations and test on untouched scenes. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: NVIDIA; UT Austin; Augmentron authors

props.What it is: Fine-tuning updates a pretrained policy using demonstrations from a new task or robot. Small adapters such as LoRA can reduce the number of trainable weights, but the action interface, normalization and camera setup must still match the target system.
props.Prerequisites: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs); dataset splits; GPU training basics
props.Frontier state 2026: openpi documents policy adaptation and LoRA configurations; LeRobot documents SmolVLA and NVIDIA releases GR00T models. Compare adapter and full tuning under equal data budgets; support for one embodiment is not evidence for another. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Physical Intelligence; Hugging Face; NVIDIA

props.What it is: A learned policy may need longer to compute than the robot can safely wait between commands. Scheduling overlaps computation with execution and decides how to join action chunks without sending stale or discontinuous commands.
props.Prerequisites: Action chunking; timestamps; queues; safe command limits
props.Frontier state 2026: RTC and LeRobot asynchronous inference address policy latency at the action queue level, not embedded hardware design. A 2026 control-aware scheduling preprint extends this direction; quantization is only an optional hypothesis until accuracy and timing are measured. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Physical Intelligence; Hugging Face; control-aware command generation authors

props.What it is: A language or vision-language model can choose a sequence of existing robot skills or write code that calls them. This is a high-level decision layer, not a replacement for a controller that knows how to move safely.
props.Prerequisites: Planning basics; API contracts; sandboxing; robot skill interfaces
props.Frontier state 2026: SayCan grounds skill selection in feasibility and Code as Policies composes perception/action APIs. This node studies grounding and executable contracts, not another generic long-horizon manipulation pipeline; generated code must never bypass a safety gate. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Google Research; Code as Policies and SayCan authors

props.What it is: Cross-embodiment learning shares experience between robots with different bodies, sensors or command spaces. The challenge is deciding what can transfer without pretending that two robots have identical joints, reach or capabilities.
props.Prerequisites: Robot datasets & benchmarks; action spaces; normalization; multi-task learning
props.Frontier state 2026: Open X-Embodiment/RT-X demonstrates shared-data benefits; CrossFormer handles heterogeneous inputs and action heads. Transfer must be tested on held-out embodiments, not just held-out episodes from a robot seen during training. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Open X-Embodiment collaboration; UC Berkeley; CMU

props.What it is: Self-improvement alternates collecting experience and updating a policy instead of freezing it after one training run. Continual learning additionally asks whether new skills can be acquired without erasing older ones.
props.Prerequisites: Offline reinforcement learning; evaluation; replay buffers; safe rollback
props.Frontier state 2026: RoboCat demonstrates an iterative self-generated-data loop; RLPD combines prior data with online reinforcement learning. These are reference ingredients, not proof of unattended lifelong operation; gate each update on retained-skill tests and keep human-approved rollback. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Google DeepMind; UC Berkeley RLPD authors

knowledge.name: Failure detection & uncertainty for learned policies

props.What it is: A failure monitor estimates whether execution is going wrong and decides when to stop or ask for help. Uncertainty is useful only if it predicts real mistakes; a confident model can still be wrong in a new scene.
props.Prerequisites: Probability; calibration; held-out data; safe stopping interface
props.Frontier state 2026: KnowNo calibrates ambiguity in language planners, not arbitrary low-level robot failures. Use separate action-level monitors and test distribution shift; conformal guarantees require their statistical assumptions and do not certify physical safety. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Princeton; Google; Stanford KnowNo authors

aliases: Failure detection & uncertainty for learned policies

props.What it is: A sensor converts a physical quantity into a number, but the number is never perfect. Accuracy is closeness to the true value, resolution is the smallest distinguishable step, and bandwidth describes how fast a signal it can follow. Characterization measures bias, repeatability and noise; Allan deviation shows how inertial noise changes with averaging time.
props.Prerequisites: Basic statistics, units and plotting; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics) for electrical acquisition.
props.Frontier state 2026: Kalibr documents white noise and slowly varying bias separately, and warns that its stationary, constant-temperature model misses temperature and scale-factor effects. Characterize the actual mounted sensor instead of treating a datasheet number as system accuracy. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ETH ASL (Kalibr); Oxford ori-drs (Allan variance ROS)

props.What it is: Proprioception measures the robot itself, such as a joint angle or wheel rotation. Incremental optical encoders count transitions and often need a reference procedure; absolute magnetic encoders report an angle within their measurement range. Mounting alignment and magnet placement matter as much as reading the digital value.
props.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics); basic angles.
props.Frontier state 2026: SimpleFOC documents quadrature and index inputs; the AS5600 breakout provides a practical contactless magnetic-angle exercise. Single-turn absolute angle is not automatically multi-turn joint position. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ams OSRAM (AS5600); Adafruit; SimpleFOC

props.What it is: An inertial measurement unit measures acceleration and angular velocity; some packages also measure magnetic field. Accelerometers respond to gravity as well as motion, gyroscopes drift when integrated, and nearby motors can disturb magnetic readings. Learn axes, units, bias and calibration here; orientation fusion and EKFs belong to State estimation & SLAM.
props.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; vectors; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics).
props.Frontier state 2026: TDK documents a six-axis ICM-42688-P, while Ceva documents the BNO085/BNO086 nine-axis package with embedded processing. Do not confuse raw inertial measurements with the package firmware’s orientation estimate. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: TDK InvenSense; Ceva and Bosch; ETH ASL

props.What it is: Force/torque transducers measure loads at a joint or wrist, including forces and twisting moments. Motor current can also estimate motor torque using a torque constant, but it is not a direct measurement of contact force at the tool. Bias, mounting loads and transmission effects must be characterized before using either signal.
props.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; basic forces and moments; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics); motor torque constants.
props.Frontier state 2026: ATI documents the Mini45 transducer and ODrive documents torque/current control. Start with a low-energy current-estimation experiment; this budget does not promise a commercial six-axis wrist transducer, and contact estimates are not safety-rated. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ATI Industrial Automation; ODrive

props.What it is: A camera turns light into pixels; a pinhole model describes how a 3D point projects onto the image. Intrinsic calibration estimates focal lengths, image center and lens distortion from known targets. Exposure, focus and shutter behavior are acquisition choices, not object-detection algorithms.
props.Prerequisites: Basic geometry and matrices; Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise.
props.Frontier state 2026: OpenCV provides checkerboard calibration and distortion models; Kalibr supports several projection and distortion models. Keep focus and resolution fixed after calibration and inspect residuals instead of assuming any successful solver output is good. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: OpenCV; ETH ASL (Kalibr)

knowledge.name: Depth cameras: stereo, structured light & ToF

props.What it is: Depth cameras report distance per pixel, rather than only color. Stereo compares two viewpoints, structured light projects a pattern, and time-of-flight measures light travel time or phase. Range, lighting, reflective surfaces and occlusion affect what is measured; scene recognition belongs to Perception.
props.Prerequisites: RGB cameras & intrinsic calibration; Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; basic triangulation.
props.Frontier state 2026: The opened D405 page describes close-range stereo; OAK-D, Gemini 2 and ZED 2 provide other stereo references. These are not ToF cameras: the physical principles are alternatives, not interchangeable product labels; full-system cost depends on host compute and the chosen model. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: RealSense; Luxonis; Orbbec; Stereolabs

aliases: Depth cameras: stereo, structured light & ToF

props.What it is: LiDAR samples distances using laser light and returns a scan or point cloud. A 2D unit covers a plane; a 3D unit covers multiple vertical directions. Learn field of view, scan pattern, reflectivity limits and timing here; map-building and localization algorithms belong to State estimation & SLAM.
props.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; coordinate frames; laser handling according to the device instructions.
props.Frontier state 2026: SLAMTEC’s RPLIDAR A1 explicitly uses laser triangulation, so not every LiDAR uses time-of-flight. Livox Mid-360 and Ouster OS1 illustrate 3D coverage; the entry budget is for a basic 2D setup, not an OS1. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: SLAMTEC; Livox; Ouster

props.What it is: Small rangefinders measure the distance to a nearby surface without forming a full image. Ultrasonic units listen for sound echoes, infrared triangulation uses reflected light geometry, and optical ToF measures a light-based delay. Beam width, blind zones, surface angle and interference determine whether a reading is useful.
props.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics).
props.Frontier state 2026: Pololu documents both a Sharp/Socle analog IR rangefinder and a VL53L1X ToF carrier. The advertised maximum range is conditional, not a guaranteed range on every surface; compare measurements against a physical ruler. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: STMicroelectronics (VL53L1X); Pololu; Sharp/Socle; Adafruit

props.What it is: Extrinsic calibration finds the rotation and translation between sensor coordinate frames. Hand-eye calibration relates a camera to a moving robot tool, while camera-IMU and camera-LiDAR calibration align different measurement types. Good motion, target visibility and a rigid mount are necessary to obtain a meaningful result.
props.Prerequisites: RGB cameras & intrinsic calibration; IMUs: accelerometers, gyroscopes & magnetometers; rigid transforms; Time synchronization & timestamping for temporal alignment.
props.Frontier state 2026: Kalibr documents spatial and temporal camera-IMU calibration and overlapping multi-camera calibration. OpenCV exposes hand-eye routines; Koide’s toolbox provides targetless camera-LiDAR calibration, but its optimization is a calibration tool here, not a new SLAM node. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ETH ASL; OpenCV; Koide and collaborators

props.What it is: Two sensors can disagree simply because they measured at different times. Timestamping records when acquisition happened; synchronization aligns clocks, while a hardware trigger can align capture events. A common clock alone does not prove simultaneous exposures or remove transport latency.
props.Prerequisites: Basic clocks and sampling; Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics).
props.Frontier state 2026: LinuxPTP implements IEEE 1588 PTP; Basler documents model-dependent PTP and trigger features. ROS Image explicitly calls for an acquisition-time timestamp, so callback arrival time must not silently substitute for exposure time. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: LinuxPTP; Basler; ROS 2 common_interfaces maintainers

props.What it is: A driver turns a device stream into messages that other programs can read. ROS sensor messages carry measurements with timestamps, coordinate frames and sometimes uncertainty; rosbag2 records messages for repeatable offline work. Check units, missing values, QoS and dropped messages before trusting a recording.
props.Prerequisites: Basic ROS 2 topics and Linux; Time synchronization & timestamping; relevant sensor modality basics.
props.Frontier state 2026: ROS Imu specifies SI units and covariance conventions, Image specifies acquisition timestamps, and sensor-data QoS trades guaranteed delivery for timely samples. image_pipeline covers camera calibration and image preparation; recording a bag does not guarantee lossless capture. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ROS 2 common_interfaces; rosbag2; ROS perception maintainers

props.What it is: A simulated sensor generates measurements from a virtual scene or robot state. Noise models deliberately add effects such as random error and bias, so software is not tested only on perfect values. Simulation helps test the acquisition pipeline but cannot certify that a real sensor behaves the same way.
props.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; ROS 2 sensor drivers, metadata & recording; basic simulation concepts.
props.Frontier state 2026: Gazebo documents IMU and LiDAR sensors and Gaussian noise with bias support; Isaac Sim documents camera, RTX and physics sensors. Validate simulated distributions and timing against real recordings before drawing sim-to-real conclusions. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Gazebo; NVIDIA Isaac Sim

props.What it is: An event camera reports individual pixel brightness changes rather than complete images at a fixed frame rate. Each event includes a pixel location, time and change polarity, so acquisition and storage differ from an ordinary video. Bias settings, lighting flicker and synchronization need characterization before downstream perception.
props.Prerequisites: RGB cameras & intrinsic calibration; Time synchronization & timestamping; ROS 2 sensor drivers, metadata & recording.
props.Frontier state 2026: Prophesee documents event-based sensing and Metavision tooling; iniVation is another neuromorphic-vision supplier. Start with recorded events: hardware pricing is unknown here, and OpenEB is the open portion of Metavision, not a claim that every SDK module or camera is open source. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Prophesee; iniVation

props.What it is: Radar transmits radio waves and measures their reflections to obtain range and motion information. Antenna layout and waveform settings affect what the hardware can resolve, while the device may expose processed detections rather than raw samples. This node covers acquisition and characterization, not object recognition or radar odometry.
props.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; sampling and basic frequency-domain concepts; ROS 2 sensor drivers, metadata & recording.
props.Frontier state 2026: TI documents the IWR6843 as a 60–64 GHz radar chip and the IWR6843ISK as an evaluation board with antennas and point-cloud access. A chip, an evaluation board and a complete raw-data capture setup are different purchases; current delivered prices are unknown. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Texas Instruments

props.What it is: Robot skin spreads contact sensors across a surface rather than relying on a single fingertip camera. Magnetic soft skins infer deformation from a magnetized elastomer near magnetic sensors; larger coverage also needs wiring, repeatable fabrication and calibration. This is about material and readout design, not tactile manipulation policies.
props.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning (Embedded & electronics); Tactile sensing for manipulation (Manipulation) as an application bridge.
props.Frontier state 2026: ReSkin separates passive skin from sensing electronics; AnySkin reports replaceable magnetic interfaces and cross-instance experiments in 2024. These are building blocks for distributed coverage, not evidence of a ready-made full-body skin or guaranteed calibration-free use on arbitrary shapes. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ReSkin authors (CMU/FAIR); AnySkin authors and collaborators

props.What it is: A microphone converts sound pressure into an electrical signal; an array records sound at several positions. Matching channel order, sample timing and microphone geometry makes the recording useful for later direction or speech processing. Motor noise, vibration and echoes should be measured rather than mistaken for useful signals.
props.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; sampling; Time synchronization & timestamping.
props.Frontier state 2026: Seeed documents a USB four-microphone ReSpeaker array; ODAS is an open C library for downstream sound localization, tracking and separation. Here ODAS is a diagnostic bridge only: audio inference algorithms belong outside the sensing taxonomy. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Seeed Studio; IntRoLab (ODAS)

props.What it is: GNSS receivers measure satellite radio signals to report outdoor position and time. RTK uses correction information from a reference system to improve positioning under suitable conditions. Antennas, sky visibility, multipath and correction availability matter; fusing GNSS with an IMU belongs to State estimation & SLAM.
props.Prerequisites: Sensor characteristics, uncertainty & noise; coordinate frames; Time synchronization & timestamping.
props.Frontier state 2026: u-blox documents the multi-band ZED-F9P family with RTK. Variant availability differs on the product page; a module is not a complete rover and centimeter-level vendor claims are conditional, not an indoor or guaranteed outdoor result. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: u-blox

props.What it is: A wrist camera moves with the tool, while external cameras give a wider view of the workspace. A useful collection rig needs rigid mounts, repeatable camera settings, calibration, synchronized observations and records of latency. The goal here is trustworthy sensor data, not a teleoperation workflow or learned robot policy.
props.Prerequisites: RGB cameras & intrinsic calibration; Extrinsic & multi-sensor calibration; Time synchronization & timestamping; ROS 2 sensor drivers, metadata & recording; Tactile sensing for manipulation only when adding touch.
props.Frontier state 2026: UMI documents a handheld gripper with a wrist-mounted GoPro and explicit latency handling; LeRobot documents camera configuration and OpenCV/RealSense camera options. A small USB-camera rig is the budget baseline, not a claim that a complete UMI or robot arm costs under €500. Snapshot of opened documentation, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: UMI authors (Stanford and collaborators); Hugging Face LeRobot

props.What it is: A simulator repeatedly computes forces, accelerations and the next state. The time step and numerical integrator decide how much error accumulates, even before the robot touches anything.
props.Prerequisites: Python; vectors; introductory differential equations
props.Frontier state 2026: Forward dynamics remains foundational; compare energy drift and wall-clock cost before trusting faster rollouts. Simulator speed claims depend on model, batch size and hardware. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Modern Robotics; Google DeepMind; MIT

props.What it is: Collision geometry tells the engine which shapes can touch; it is often simpler than the visible mesh. A contact solver estimates the forces that stop objects passing through one another, using approximations to friction and compliance.
props.Prerequisites: Forces; rigid bodies; time stepping
props.Frontier state 2026: Soft-contact and hybrid-contact models make different compromises. Newton and MuJoCo offer current implementations; matching a visually plausible stack is not proof of accurate friction or impact. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Google DeepMind; MIT Drake; Newton community

knowledge.name: Robot and scene formats: URDF, MJCF, SDF & USD

props.What it is: Robot descriptions store links, joints, masses and collision shapes; scene formats also organize environments and assets. URDF, MJCF, SDF and USD serve different workflows, so converting a file can silently lose physics settings.
props.Prerequisites: XML basics; units; coordinate transforms
props.Frontier state 2026: USD supports composition of large scenes, while MJCF includes engine-specific dynamics settings. Validate joint limits, inertias, scale and collision geometry after every importer; visual equivalence is insufficient. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ROS community; Google DeepMind; OpenUSD; Gazebo

aliases: Robot and scene formats: URDF, MJCF, SDF & USD

props.What it is: A bridge lets ROS 2 software exchange commands and sensor messages with a simulated robot. Simulation time must reach every node consistently, or apparently valid messages can be too old or from the wrong clock.
props.Prerequisites: ROS 2 topics; transforms; robot descriptions
props.Frontier state 2026: Gazebo Harmonic has a maintained ROS 2 bridge workflow. Use a supported ROS/Gazebo pairing and pin versions; Gazebo Classic tutorials are not drop-in instructions for modern Gazebo. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Gazebo community; ROS community

props.What it is: Virtual cameras, depth sensors and inertial sensors turn simulator state into the measurements a robot would receive. The engine can also provide exact labels, but perfect labels and clean images can hide problems found on real sensors.
props.Prerequisites: Camera geometry; arrays; basic sensor noise
props.Frontier state 2026: ManiSkill supports parallel visual data collection and Isaac Sim Replicator supports synthetic data workflows. Include noise, clipping, missing depth, timestamp errors and calibration rather than equating photorealism with sensor truth. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ManiSkill/SAPIEN; NVIDIA; Gazebo

props.What it is: Instead of running one world at a time, a GPU can step many copies together. A vectorized environment batches actions, observations and resets, making large robot-learning experiments practical.
props.Prerequisites: Python arrays; GPU memory; environment reset API
props.Frontier state 2026: MJX, MuJoCo Playground, Isaac Lab, ManiSkill and Genesis provide parallel workflows with different backends. Current Playground main uses PyTorch, reaf-sim and MuJoCo Warp; the original JAX/MJX environments remain on rss2025. Isaac Lab documents multiple backends. Pin a revision and measure actual throughput, compilation and rendering costs; these sources do not establish a universal speed ranking.
props.Key players: Google DeepMind; NVIDIA; ManiSkill; Genesis AI

props.What it is: Domain randomization changes lighting, geometry or physical parameters between simulated trials. The aim is robustness to uncertainty, not simply making many colorful images.
props.Prerequisites: Train/test splits; parameter distributions; basic evaluation
props.Frontier state 2026: Visual randomization has established primary evidence, but a wider distribution can also make learning harder. Treat the LeRobot low-cost transfer wedge as a hypothesis: estimate realistic ranges and reserve unseen combinations for evaluation. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Domain randomization authors; NVIDIA; ManiSkill

props.What it is: System identification estimates unknown physical parameters from measured motion. Calibrating a simulator means checking that its masses, friction, delays and actuator behavior predict observations not used during fitting.
props.Prerequisites: Regression; time series; safe joint operation for real trials
props.Frontier state 2026: Contact and actuator parameters may compensate for one another, so a good training fit can be misleading. Begin with identifiable toy models and held-out trajectories before adjusting an entire robot. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: MIT Drake; Google DeepMind; LeRobot community

props.What it is: A digital twin reconstructs a particular real workspace for repeatable experiments. Gaussian splatting can reproduce how that workspace looks from new viewpoints, but rendering primitives do not automatically provide collision geometry or material physics.
props.Prerequisites: Multi-view geometry; camera calibration; contact simulation
props.Frontier state 2026: The 2025 real-to-sim soft-body evaluation paper couples physics-informed reconstruction and Gaussian rendering. Its reported policy correlations are task-specific evidence, not proof that any photorealistic twin predicts real success. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Real-to-Sim Robot Policy Evaluation authors; SimplerEnv authors

props.What it is: A learned simulator predicts future observations from past observations and actions instead of solving all physics equations. Its predictions can be useful for testing, but plausible videos can still ignore an action or invent physically impossible outcomes.
props.Prerequisites: Deep learning; sequence models; held-out rollouts
props.Frontier state 2026: DreamerV3 supplies a reproducible latent-model baseline; the 2026 BWM paper proposes action-conditioned robotic simulation. Validate action sensitivity, state consistency and error growth, not just image scores; no universal substitute for physics is established here. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: DreamerV3 authors; Boundless World Model authors

props.What it is: A benchmark defines tasks, resets, success rules and reporting so experiments can be compared. A simulation score is evidence about those settings, not a certificate of real-world competence.
props.Prerequisites: Statistics; experiment tracking; environment APIs
props.Frontier state 2026: ManiSkill, RoboCasa and SimplerEnv cover complementary task and transfer-evaluation settings. Keep assets, seeds, horizons, success criteria and reset rules fixed; report failed runs and avoid leaking evaluation conditions into training. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: ManiSkill; RoboCasa; SimplerEnv

knowledge.name: Procedural scenes, asset pipelines & task generation

props.What it is: Procedural generation creates varied environments from reusable rules and assets. Useful robot scenes need valid scales, collision shapes and reachable task states, not merely attractive layouts.
props.Prerequisites: Scene graphs; geometry; random seeds; asset licenses
props.Frontier state 2026: RoboCasa provides large-scale household environments and Isaac Sim Replicator supports variation. Generated tasks require solvability and collision checks plus license provenance; quantity alone does not guarantee useful diversity. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: RoboCasa; NVIDIA; OpenUSD

aliases: Procedural scenes, asset pipelines & task generation

props.What it is: Differentiable simulation computes how changing a parameter or action changes a later outcome. Those gradients can help optimization, but collisions and changing contact modes can make them unstable or misleading.
props.Prerequisites: Calculus; automatic differentiation; numerical simulation
props.Frontier state 2026: Warp kernels support differentiation, but a framework using Warp does not guarantee differentiable physics. MJX documentation explicitly says MJX-Warp does not support automatic differentiation; choose a supported differentiable solver or smooth custom Warp kernels and validate gradients against finite differences. Brax maintains training rather than its old simulation environments, recommending Playground and MJX/MuJoCo Warp for simulation. That maintenance recommendation is not evidence of gradient support.
props.Key players: NVIDIA Warp; Newton community; MIT

props.What it is: Deformable simulators model objects that bend or flow rather than staying rigid. Cloth, soft solids and particles require different approximations, and coupling them to rigid robots can be expensive and sensitive to settings.
props.Prerequisites: Continuum-mechanics intuition; contact; numerical stability
props.Frontier state 2026: Genesis describes a multiphysics platform; Newton and Isaac Lab expose additional solver workflows. This node concerns simulation fidelity and coupling, not the manipulation pilot node about learning to handle deformable objects. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
props.Key players: Genesis contributors / Genesis AI support; Newton community; NVIDIA; real-to-sim evaluation authors

props.What it is: A robot cannot read its true position directly; it maintains a belief about possible states. Probability distributions and covariance describe both the best guess and how uncertain it is.
props.Prerequisites: Python, vectors, basic probability; distinguish state from measurement.
props.Frontier state 2026: Bayes filtering remains the foundation beneath modern estimators. Correct uncertainty and correlated measurements matter as much as a smooth-looking trajectory. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Groningen robotics course; PythonRobotics contributors; Springer SLAM authors

props.What it is: Dead reckoning estimates motion by adding up wheel rotations or inertial measurements over time. Small wheel-slip or sensor-bias errors accumulate, so this is a short-term reference rather than a permanent global position.
props.Prerequisites: Planar coordinate transforms, velocity integration, timestamps; basic sensor noise.
props.Frontier state 2026: Modern Robotics explains the wheel-to-chassis integration used in practical mobile bases. Contemporary fusion still needs explicit bias and wheel-slip tests; inertial integration alone does not stop drift. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Lynch and Park; ROBOTIS; robot_localization maintainers

props.What it is: A Kalman filter alternates motion predictions with sensor corrections, weighting each by uncertainty. EKF linearizes nonlinear models, while UKF propagates selected sample points through them.
props.Prerequisites: Bayesian state estimation & uncertainty; Jacobians, covariance; wheel/inertial motion models.
props.Frontier state 2026: ROS robot_localization exposes EKF and UKF with configurable sensor inputs and timeouts. Reliable fusion needs consistent frames, realistic covariance and avoidance of double-counted data; a filter does not create absolute information. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Charles River Analytics / robot_localization community; GTSAM; Groningen

props.What it is: A particle filter represents possible robot poses as many weighted guesses. Unlike a single Gaussian, it can keep several plausible locations in a repeated corridor and recover after being moved unexpectedly.
props.Prerequisites: Bayesian state estimation & uncertainty; sampling, sensor likelihoods, occupancy maps.
props.Frontier state 2026: Particle methods remain useful when localization beliefs have multiple peaks. Their cost grows with state dimension, and global recovery must be tested separately from easy tracking near a known start. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Springer SLAM authors; PythonRobotics contributors

props.What it is: A factor graph connects unknown poses to noisy constraints such as odometry or landmark observations. Solving the graph adjusts a whole trajectory together instead of only correcting the newest pose.
props.Prerequisites: Least squares, Jacobians, rigid transforms, covariance; Bayesian state estimation & uncertainty.
props.Frontier state 2026: GTSAM supports factor-graph inference and IMU preintegration.
