RSS 2025 includes certifiable optimization work, but offline bundle-adjustment guarantees do not imply every real-time SLAM graph is globally solved. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Frank Dellaert / Borglab; Georgia Tech; MIT SPARK; Harvard computational robotics researchers

props.What it is: An estimator needs to know where sensors sit and when each measurement was taken. Observability asks which quantities the available motion and measurements can actually determine, such as whether absolute yaw or scale is knowable.
props.Prerequisites: Rigid transforms, camera geometry, Jacobians, Kalman filtering & multisensor fusion.
props.Frontier state 2026: Kalibr solves camera/IMU spatial and temporal calibration; OpenVINS supports online calibration components. LaMAria shows that calibration can vary over long sessions; good residuals alone do not prove all parameters are identifiable. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking. Continuous-time trajectory models and preintegration are advanced extensions, especially when sensors sample asynchronously.
props.Key players: ETH Zurich ASL; OpenVINS / Patrick Geneva and collaborators; ETH CVG

props.What it is: Visual odometry tracks camera motion through images; adding an IMU helps through fast motion and short visual gaps. SLAM additionally reuses places and maps to correct accumulated drift, which plain odometry does not do.
props.Prerequisites: Camera geometry; Estimator calibration, timing & observability; filtering or factor graphs.
props.Frontier state 2026: ORB-SLAM3 supplies visual/inertial multi-map SLAM and OpenVINS a filter-based VIO baseline. LaMAria 2025 highlights city-scale failures; monocular-only metric scale and inertial initialization need explicit treatment. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: University of Zaragoza SLAMLab; OpenVINS; ETH CVG

props.What it is: A planar laser measures distances around a mobile robot; matching scans estimates its motion. An occupancy grid records which floor-plan cells appear free or blocked, while graph optimization keeps repeated visits aligned.
props.Prerequisites: Wheel & inertial dead reckoning; occupancy probabilities, ROS messages and transforms.
props.Frontier state 2026: SLAM Toolbox documents ROS 2 mapping, graph serialization, localization and lifelong-map workflows. A flat laser map is a useful baseline, not a complete representation of stairs, overhangs or moving people. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Steve Macenski; ROS 2 navigation community; ROBOTIS

props.What it is: A 3D lidar records clouds of surface points, which can be aligned to estimate motion. IMU fusion helps undo motion during a scan and bridge weak geometry; global loop closure is a separate component.
props.Prerequisites: Point-cloud registration, SE(3), inertial bias, calibration; filtering and factor graphs.
props.Frontier state 2026: KISS-ICP is a simple lidar-only odometry reference, FAST-LIO2 a filter-based LIO reference, and LIO-SAM a smoothing-based alternative. FAST-LIVO2 released code in 2025 for lidar/IMU/camera fusion; more sensors bring synchronization and compute risks. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: University of Bonn; HKU MARS; Tixiao Shan and collaborators

props.What it is: Place recognition proposes that a robot has returned somewhere familiar. Geometric verification checks that guess before adding a loop constraint; relocalization recovers a pose after tracking was lost.
props.Prerequisites: Visual or lidar odometry; Factor graphs, smoothing & pose-graph SLAM; feature matching.
props.Frontier state 2026: ORB-SLAM3 and RTAB-Map provide practical map-reuse and loop-closure references. Learned matching priors such as MASt3R broaden experiments, but look-alike scenes still demand geometric checks and false-positive reporting. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: University of Zaragoza; IntRoLab; NAVER LABS

props.What it is: People, moved furniture and changing lighting can make old map assumptions wrong. Robust estimation rejects bad constraints and tracks when a map or pose is no longer trustworthy instead of silently reporting success.
props.Prerequisites: Place recognition, loop closure & relocalization; Kalman filtering & multisensor fusion; failure metrics.
props.Frontier state 2026: DynaSLAM is an older dynamic-scene teaching baseline, not a 2026 leaderboard winner. SLAM Toolbox supports persistent mapping and LaMAria exposes long-session challenges; dependable recovery and map-version policies remain important research questions. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: IntRoLab; SLAM Toolbox maintainers; ETH CVG; Zaragoza dynamic-SLAM researchers

props.What it is: A dense map models surfaces throughout a scene instead of only a sparse set of landmarks. Semantic labels add meaning, while neural priors and Gaussian splats can create detailed reconstructions; visual realism alone does not establish metric accuracy.
props.Prerequisites: Visual odometry & visual-inertial SLAM; GPU programming basics; map representations and evaluation.
props.Frontier state 2026: SplaTAM (CVPR 2024) uses RGB-D Gaussian maps, MASt3R-SLAM (CVPR 2025) uses learned reconstruction priors, and PINGS (RSS 2025) couples radiance and distance fields. Hardware speed, monocular scale, dynamic objects and noncommercial prior licenses must be checked before deployment. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking. ScaRF-SLAM (RA-L 2026) separates classical tracking from learned dense reconstruction; the November 2026 Map2SLAM preprint instead makes streaming model outputs revisable through persistent SLAM state. These are different design choices, not proof that one dominates on lab hardware.
props.Key players: Imperial Dyson Robotics Lab; NAVER LABS; SplaTAM authors; Bonn/PRBonn; MIT SPARK
props.Sources:
https://github.com/spla-tam/SplaTAM
https://github.com/rmurai0610/MASt3R-SLAM
https://github.com/naver/mast3r
https://www.roboticsproceedings.org/rss21/p040.html
https://github.com/MIT-SPARK/Kimera-Multi
http://introlab.github.io/rtabmap/
https://github.com/ori-drs/ScaRF-SLAM
https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11169

props.What it is: Several robots can combine partial maps if they discover which places they share and align their coordinate frames. Distributed methods exchange information without assuming every sensor stream can reach one central computer.
props.Prerequisites: Factor graphs, smoothing & pose-graph SLAM; loop verification; networking and distributed systems.
props.Frontier state 2026: Kimera-Multi documents peer-to-peer robust mapping with inter-robot loop closures. Its ROS Noetic-era build is a reproducibility risk; network dropout, duplicate evidence and incorrect cross-robot matches need explicit tests. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking. The index README still marks its Remote Topic Manager component as coming soon; a complete peer-to-peer reproduction must verify component availability first, not assume a one-command build. CU-Multi (2025) specifically cautions that splitting a single trajectory can miss realistic pose-dependent multi-robot observations.
props.Key players: MIT SPARK / Luca Carlone; Kimera-Multi collaborators

props.What it is: Evaluation compares estimated trajectories with an independent reference and records when tracking fails. Absolute and relative errors answer different questions; alignment, time association and uncertainty calibration can otherwise hide mistakes.
props.Prerequisites: Basic statistics, coordinate transforms; Bayesian state estimation & uncertainty.
props.Frontier state 2026: evo and TUM provide established trajectory tools; LaMAria and the RSS 2025 workshop motivate long-session and failure-aware tests beyond one average ATE. Report runtime, tracking coverage and alignment rules as well as accuracy. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Michael Grupp; TUM CVG; ETH CVG; RSS visual-SLAM workshop organizers

props.What it is: A legged robot can estimate its body motion using an IMU plus joint kinematics and feet believed to be stationary. Invariant filters exploit rotation and translation structure, but a slipping foot is not a reliable fixed landmark.
props.Prerequisites: Kalman filtering & multisensor fusion; Lie groups; forward kinematics and contact assumptions.
props.Frontier state 2026: The contact-aided InEKF has an open implementation and RSS theory; GTSAM documentation includes 2026 proprioceptive-estimation material. Absolute position and gravity-axis yaw are not observable from contact/IMU alone; good filtering cannot remove that ambiguity. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: Ross Hartley; University of Michigan; Barrau and Bonnabel; Borglab / Seoul National University

props.What it is: GNSS gives an outdoor position reference that can limit dead-reckoning drift. Fusion must translate latitude and longitude into a consistent local frame and account for heading, antenna placement and unreliable fixes near buildings.
props.Prerequisites: Kalman filtering & multisensor fusion; frames and covariances; geographic versus local coordinates.
props.Frontier state 2026: robot_localization navsat_transform documents GPS, IMU heading and odometry inputs, including ENU/UTM conventions. LIO-SAM accepts GPS constraints; neither system turns bad multipath fixes into guaranteed centimeter accuracy. Evidence snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive late-2026 ranking.
props.Key players: robot_localization community; Charles River Analytics; LIO-SAM authors; Borglab
Physical Intelligence, NVIDIA, Google DeepMind, Hugging Face, Xiaomi
props.Project ideas: Fine-tune SmolVLA on our own dataset; compare SmolVLA vs π0.5 on the same task; run a VLA in real time on a laptop GPU
props.What it is: Robot foundation models: a vision-language model (like the ones behind chatbots) extended to output robot actions. You give it a camera image and an instruction ('put the cup in the sink') and it outputs motor commands.
props.Frontier state 2026: Open models are fine-tunable on cheap arms (SmolVLA, π0/π0.5 via LeRobot, GR00T). 2026 research focuses on efficiency (1-bit and real-time VLAs on consumer GPUs), memory for long tasks, and scaling to 100k+ hours of real data (Xiaomi).
props.Prerequisites: Transformers, VLM fine-tuning, imitation learning

props.Key players: NVIDIA, ETH Zurich, UC Berkeley
props.Project ideas: Train a cube-picking policy in sim, then fine-tune on the real arm with HIL-SERL
props.What it is: The robot learns by trial and error from a reward signal, usually in simulation where failures cost nothing. Dominant for locomotion (walking robots); increasingly combined with imitation learning for manipulation.
props.Best resources: Isaac Lab, ManiSkill, MuJoCo Playground; HIL-SERL in LeRobot
props.Frontier state 2026: Massively parallel GPU simulation makes sim RL cheap; human-in-the-loop RL (HIL-SERL) brings RL to real arms. RL fine-tuning of VLAs is an active research topic.
props.Prerequisites: RL basics (PPO, SAC), a physics simulator

props.Key players: Advanced Machine Intelligence (Paris), Meta (V-JEPA 2), NVIDIA, Google DeepMind
props.Project ideas: Natural follow-up to the AI Lab's JEPA bootcamp: train a small latent world model on our SO-101 dataset and use it for planning
props.What it is: Models that learn to predict how the world will evolve (e.g. the next video frames, or an abstract representation of them) and use that prediction to choose actions. The bet: a robot that can 'imagine' consequences generalizes better.
props.Best resources: V-JEPA 2 paper; recent world-action-model papers on arXiv
props.Frontier state 2026: Hottest research direction of 2026: 'world action models' unify video prediction and action, JEPA-style latent world models are being plugged into VLAs. Paris has a major player: Advanced Machine Intelligence, which raised close to €890M in 2026.
props.Prerequisites: Self-supervised learning, video models, JEPA concepts

props.Key players: Hugging Face, NVIDIA (Isaac Teleop), Bleu Robotics
props.Project ideas: Build a lab data-collection station and publish a dataset on the Hub; VR teleop for SO-101
props.What it is: The tooling to let a human drive a robot (leader arm, VR headset, phone) while recording synchronized video and joint data. In modern robotics, data is the bottleneck, so whoever collects good data fast wins.
props.Frontier state 2026: Standardized dataset formats (LeRobotDataset on the HF Hub) and cheap leader/follower arms. Startups compete on deployment speed: e.g. Bleu Robotics claims new tasks from \~10 demonstrations.
props.Prerequisites: Python, cameras, serial/USB communication basics

props.Key players: Academic labs; several Chinese robotics teams
props.Project ideas: Turn smartphone videos of lab members into SO-101 training data
props.What it is: Using videos of humans doing tasks (YouTube, egocentric cameras) to train robots, instead of expensive robot demonstrations. Requires detecting hand poses and translating them into robot motions.
props.Frontier state 2026: 'Data engines' that retarget human hand motions onto robots and composite robot arms into videos measurably improve real-robot success; egocentric-video pretraining is a growing family of models.
props.Prerequisites: Computer vision (pose estimation, segmentation), imitation learning

props.Key players: Stanford (ACT/ALOHA), Columbia/TRI (Diffusion Policy), Hugging Face LeRobot
props.Project ideas: Train an SO-101 to sort objects by color; pick-and-place with distractors; benchmark ACT vs Diffusion Policy with 20/50/100 demos
props.What it is: Teach a robot by showing it: a human performs the task (usually by teleoperation), the robot records camera images and joint positions, and a neural network learns to map what it sees to what it should do. It's supervised learning where the labels are actions.
props.Best resources: LeRobot docs + tutorials; ACT and Diffusion Policy papers
props.Frontier state 2026: Mature workhorse. ACT and Diffusion Policy are the standard baselines; most teams now fine-tune a pretrained VLA instead of training from scratch. Open problem: generalization beyond the demonstrated setup.
props.Prerequisites: PyTorch, basic CNNs/transformers. No control theory needed to start.

props.Key players: Hugging Face, Google DeepMind (Open X-Embodiment), academic labs
props.Project ideas: Publish a clean, well-documented 42AI dataset; reproduce a paper's benchmark number
props.What it is: Shared datasets and standard test suites that let teams compare robot policies fairly. Knowing them tells you what 'state of the art' means in numbers.
props.Frontier state 2026: Community datasets on the HF Hub keep growing (including SO-101 data); simulated benchmarks like SimplerEnv and LIBERO are standard for VLA papers.
props.Prerequisites: None beyond ML basics

props.Key players: NVIDIA, Hugging Face, ETH Zurich
props.Project ideas: Sim-to-real bottle-to-basket task; measure success rate with and without domain randomization
props.What it is: Training in simulation and making the policy still work on the real robot, despite differences in physics, lighting and sensor noise (the 'reality gap'). Techniques include domain randomization and digital twins.
props.Best resources: Isaac Sim SO-101 workshop repos; LeIsaac
props.Frontier state 2026: Digital twins of low-cost arms exist (SO-101 in Isaac Sim, MuJoCo); NVIDIA runs public sim-to-real workshops on the SO-101. Generative video/world models increasingly used to produce synthetic training data.
props.Prerequisites: Simulation basics, RL or imitation learning

props.What they build: Maker of the cheapest widely sold legged robots: Go2 robot dog (from $1,600), R1 humanoid (from $4,900), G1 humanoid (from $13.5K), H1/H2 full-size humanoids, B2/A2 industrial quadrupeds, dexterous hands and LiDARs. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in Aug 2026 (IPO priced at ~61bn yuan / ~$9bn valuation).

Humanoid and service-robot company: Walker S2 industrial humanoid with autonomous hot-swappable battery, in mass production since Nov 2025 with orders reported above 800m yuan; also education and consumer robots. Signed a cooperation deal with Airbus in Jan 2026.

Founded 2023; world's largest humanoid shipper in H1 2026 per industry data cited by Global Times. Builds humanoids (A-series, X-series) and open-sources robot-learning assets: the AgiBot World dataset and the GO-1 foundation model. Began Hong Kong IPO process in Jul 2026; Oct 2026 round reported at ~RMB 50bn valuation.

Wheeled humanoid robots (G1, S1, ET1) driven by its own embodied foundation models (AstraBrain series). Raised ~$362M in early 2026 (investors incl. National AI Industry Investment Fund, Sinopec), described as China's highest-valued unlisted humanoid firm.

Started in rehabilitation robotics and now builds GR-series humanoids; ranked 6th globally in 2025 humanoid shipments (Omdia). In 2026 built Meta's 'Max' humanoid in ~3 months. Investors include SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Prosperity7.
EV maker XPeng's robotics unit; its IRON general-purpose humanoid rolled off a dedicated production line in Sep 2026 (core process automation >80%).

Collaborative robot arms (CR/CRA/Nova series), education desktop arms (Magician, Magician E6, MG400), the X-Trainer teleoperation platform for AI data collection, and ATOM full-size industrial humanoid (third batch launched Feb 2026, mass delivery targeted for 2026).

Mobile robot bases (SCOUT, RANGER, BUNKER, HUNTER, LIMO) and low-cost arms for physical-AI research: PiPER 6-DoF arm (4.2 kg, 1.5 kg payload, ±0.1 mm, ~$2,499), NERO, Cobot Magic / Mobile ALOHA kits, Pika data-collection kit. Open SDKs on GitHub.
Quadruped robots (Jueying Lite3, X30, LYNX M20 wheel-legged), DR02 all-weather humanoid and J-series joint modules; filed for a 2.5bn-yuan STAR Market IPO in May 2026.

Wheeled dual-arm R1 robots (from $39,999), LEMO A1Z 6-DoF arm (from $2,999) and LEMO desktop dual-arm platform, plus open-source VLA models (G0, G0.5) in the GalaxeaVLA repo. Raised a 1bn-yuan Series B in Feb 2026 (10bn-yuan valuation).
Tsinghua University spinout building STAR1 and L7 humanoids and dexterous hands; raised ~500m yuan Series A in Jul 2025.
KUAVO humanoid series (KUAVO 4Pro, KUAVO 5) sold as research/education and service platforms; filed for a ChiNext IPO in May 2026 (2.6bn-yuan target).

ecosystem.name: Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics (X-Humanoid)

props.What they build: State-backed humanoid innovation center: Tiangong humanoids (TianGong 3.0 in mass delivery H2 2026), embodied-AI software, and the open RoboMIND dataset (300k+ dual-arm trajectories, 700+ tasks; 20m downloads by Sep 2026).

aliases: Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics (X-Humanoid)

props.What they build: Non-profit AI institute; releases open embodied-AI 'brain' models such as RoboBrain 2.0 (7B checkpoint on Hugging Face, Jun 2025) and later RoboBrain 2.5, trained with its FlagScale framework.
Major state AI lab whose InternRobotics group open-sources InternVLA-M1 (spatially guided VLA, MIT license) and the InternUtopia (ex-GRUtopia) embodied-AI simulation platform.
Warehouse robotics: shelf/tote/pallet AMRs, sorting robots, picking robot arm and fleet software; listed in Hong Kong in Jul 2025.
Leading domestic industrial-robot and servo maker (called 'first share of industrial robots'); in Sep 2026 consolidated a humanoid robot business by acquiring Estun Kuozhuo.
Annual Beijing robotics expo and conference; 2026 edition (19-23 Aug) showed 3,000+ products. Shares the season with the World Humanoid Robot Games (2nd edition Aug 2026).
Shanghai's annual AI conference; 2026 edition (17-20 Jul) had 1,100+ exhibitors and 3,000+ products, with humanoid robots and VLA/world models as a central theme.
Top Chinese university for robotics/embodied AI; source of spinouts such as RobotEra; its Youth2Real team won two tracks at ICRA 2026 manipulation competitions.

German motion-technology supplier of bearings and drives, including actuators (motor, gearbox and sensing combined into a robot joint). In August 2026 it announced formed strain wave gearboxes for humanoid joints, with mass production planned for 2027. Its May 2026 agreement with UK robot maker Humanoid targets a four-digit number of robots deployed by 2032 and a seven-digit actuator supply commitment; these are staged future commitments, not completed deliveries.

Swiss maker of precision DC and brushless motors, gearheads, encoders and motor controllers. At Automate 2026 it demonstrated an IP67 integrated drive and humanoid joint actuators combining motors, gearboxes, encoders and control electronics. Its Young Engineers Program offers selected student teams subsidized prices or product sponsorship; eligibility is not guaranteed.
props.Warm contact path: unknown; public application route: maxon Young Engineers Program (not a warm introduction)

props.What they build: German maker of strain wave gears and precision drive systems for robotics, medical equipment, aerospace and space. A strain wave gear uses an elastically deforming gear element to obtain high reduction ratios in a compact joint; the company markets zero-backlash gear products. No market-share claim is established here.
German family company for grippers, toolholding and workholding. In 2026 it signed a partnership with Bosch Robotics to co-design an industrial-grade robot hand for humanoid robots.

German family-owned automation supplier headquartered in Esslingen am Neckar. It provides pneumatic and electric drive technologies, automation software and AI solutions, while Festo Didactic supplies technical education and training systems.

German motion-plastics supplier of self-lubricating bearings, cable chains and automation components. Its ReBeL cobot arms form part of Iggy Rob, a wheeled mobile manipulator announced in 2025 with two arms, bionic hands, lidar and 3D cameras. The 2025 coverage cited an intended price of €47,999 (about $54,500 then), not a verified current quote. In June 2026 igus announced the Iggy Rob Home service variant from €55,000; that is a different variant and price from the 2025 industrial announcement.
Danish maker of end-of-arm tooling for cobots: electric and vacuum grippers, force/torque sensors, tool changers, plus D:PLOY software for palletizing, CNC tending and packaging.

German chipmaker supplying power semiconductors, microcontrollers, sensors, connectivity and safety/security components for robots. Its Infineon Mobile Robot (IMR) demonstrates these subsystems. AdapTronics won its 2026 humanoid robotics startup challenge; Reuters reported a March 2026 Nvidia partnership covering robot hardware and digital-twin development.

Franco-Italian chipmaker headquartered in Geneva, supplying STM32 microcontrollers, MEMS motion sensors and motor-control electronics. In 2026 it acquired a stake in RoBee builder Oversonic Robotics. Reuters reported its March 2026 Nvidia partnership focused on connecting camera and motion sensors to Nvidia-based robot systems; this is not evidence that ST builds RoBee.

Dutch chipmaker: processors, sensing (radar, vision, UWB), Ethernet/TSN and CAN networking, security and functional safety for drones, AMRs and humanoids. Announced physical-AI work with Nvidia in Mar 2026.

Dutch edge-AI chip startup. Its Metis chip (~214 TOPS at ~10 W) uses digital in-memory computing to run vision models on robots and cameras. Raised more than $250M in Feb 2026 (led by Innovation Industries, with BlackRock and Samsung Catalyst).

Italian electronics and software platform, now a Qualcomm subsidiary, known for open-source microcontroller boards and the Arduino development environment. Its 2026 VENTUNO Q pairs a Qualcomm Dragonwing IQ8 processor (up to 40 dense TOPS of AI compute) with an STM32H5 microcontroller for real-time control. Arduino boards were already used in robots before this dedicated robotics product.
UK maker of low-cost Arm single-board computers (Raspberry Pi 5), Pico microcontroller boards (RP2 chips), cameras and add-on boards; widely used as the 'brain' of hobby and student robots.
German industrial sensor maker: safety laser scanners, lidar, 2D/3D vision and other sensors used on AMRs and in factory automation.

UK maker of the Shadow Dexterous Hand (tendon-driven, five-fingered research hand with tactile fingertips) and the DEX-EE hand. In Oct 2026 it started a six-month project with Fraunhofer IFF on dexterous hands, tactile sensing and teleoperation for manufacturing.
Swiss ETH spin-off making compact 6-axis force-torque sensors (MiniONE, Rokubi, SensONE, LaxONE) with integrated electronics and IMU, plus tactile sensors, so robots can 'feel' contact forces.

German provider of integrated servo drives, motion-control electronics and functional safety for robotics. In August 2026 it announced a partnership with Stabilus to develop and manufacture integrated humanoid joint actuators. The partners target scalable production; the announcement does not establish that the joint product line is already shipping.

Zurich physical-AI startup, legally Eta Robotics AG, developing force-aware dexterous manipulation. Rather than relying only on vision or fingertip sensors, it captures force information through actuators and redesigns the hardware-to-model stack. It emerged from stealth in October 2026 with a reported $30M pre-seed round from redalpine, Notion Capital, firstminute and angels including Arthur Mensch and Yann LeCun.

Budapest startup developing 3D Tissue Braiding to manufacture compliant robot bodies. It produces a scaffold, braids soft tissues and routes tendons, then connects actuators: this is not a claim that motors emerge fully assembled from the braiding step. Its investor confirmed a $7.2M pre-seed in February 2026, including individual angels from OpenAI and Hugging Face, not corporate investment by those companies.

Italian startup developing electro-adhesive gripping interfaces with tactile feedback. Its proprietary thin-film Electro Active Adhesive Layer (EAAL) is mounted on a conformable backing and activated by a 24 V electronic unit to hold objects without suction or fingers. It won Infineon’s 2026 humanoid robotics Startup Challenge; suitability for a specific object still needs testing.

German carmaker and Europe's most visible buyer of humanoid robots. After using Figure AI humanoids (Figure 02, then Figure 03 since June 2026) in its US plant Spartanburg, it started Europe's first humanoid pilot in a car plant at Leipzig in 2026 with Hexagon Robotics' wheeled AEON humanoid, delivering parts to the line in battery and component production. Runs a new competence centre for AI + robotics integration.

German carmaker testing Apptronik's Apollo humanoid robots for intralogistics (moving parts and modules to assembly workers) at the Mercedes-Benz Digital Factory Campus in Berlin-Marienfelde. Workers teach the robots by teleoperation and augmented reality (a human remotely drives the robot to record demonstrations). Mercedes also invested in Apptronik.

Europe's largest online fashion retailer and a major buyer of AI picking robots. Installing up to 50 Nomagic 'Richard' item-picking robots in its European fulfilment centres (2026) and using Sereact dual-arm robots to sort returns at Ceva Logistics sites in Germany and Poland; also invested in Sereact's Series B.

German logistics group. Its contract-logistics arm DHL Supply Chain has deployed more than 8,000 robotic systems worldwide (picking, packing, put-away) since its first robotics bet in 2017, and uses SVT Robotics' SOFTBOT platform as one integration layer to plug many robot vendors into its warehouse software.

UK online-grocery tech company that designs and installs fully robotic warehouses for retailers worldwide: a grid where swarms of 'bots' (more than 17,000 in its sites) fetch storage boxes, plus robotic picking arms. In July 2026 it won a deal to build a robotic warehouse for an unnamed European retailer (site due to go live in its 2028 financial year).

German automation giant: makes the PLCs, digital-twin and fleet software that factories use to plug robots in (Siemens Xcelerator), and is itself a test customer. In 2025-26 it ran a proof of concept with UK startup Humanoid's wheeled HMND 01 robot moving totes to a conveyor at its Erlangen electronics factory (60 tote moves/hour, 8h+ uptime).

European aircraft maker with big French operations (Toulouse). Created an in-house 'Airbus Robotics' unit in 2023 that builds its own shop-floor robots (e.g. the 4 kg CabinMarker for seat-track installation, FlexTrack drilling robot, exoskeletons) and bought UBTech's Walker S2 humanoid in 2026 for aviation-manufacturing trials.

Italian robotics system integrator (formerly Stellantis' captive supplier, now independent) that designs turnkey automated production lines, EV battery lines and also sells its own robots and cobots. In Oct 2026 it partnered with NVIDIA to run Isaac Sim digital twins and Jetson AI compute inside its robot controllers; after leaving Stellantis it is expanding into battery recycling/storage and warehouse logistics.

Austrian warehouse-automation integrator: shuttles, bots, pocket sorters, AMRs and AI picking robots plus warehouse software. Its AI-vision Pick-it-Easy Robot (~450 picks/hour) was added in 2026 to Edeka's fresh-meat centre in Germany; it opened a Robotics & AI Innovation Hub near Boston (KNAPPRobotics.ai).

German family-owned intralogistics group: storage, conveying, picking systems and warehouse software. In April 2026 it integrated its fully automatic 'SSI Piece Picking' robot into Würth Industrie Service's logistics centre in Bad Mergentheim; won several 2026 materialfluss product awards.

Austrian warehouse-automation integrator (50+ years) building shuttle systems (FlashPick) and the RovoFlex AI picking robot with camera system and PickCenter software; customer references include Dinosol and Kärcher.

Swiss warehouse-automation integrator (part of KUKA): pallet high-bay warehouses, AutoStore cube storage, robotic case and item picking (ItemPiQ robot, up to 1,000 items/hour) and healthcare/hospital automation. Delivered the AutoStore system that Cognibotics' picking cell works with at Nowaste Logistics (Sweden).
Dutch integrator of logistics automation for airports (baggage handling, robotic loading) and parcel/warehouse sites; since April 2026 part of Toyota Automated Logistics (Toyota Industries).

German builder of car paint shops and final-assembly lines; has sold 20,000+ painting robots. Its 4th-generation EcoRP4 paint robot entered production in 2026 (20,000th robot delivered to Ford Valencia).

German tech group whose supply-chain business sells warehouse software and automation. In Oct 2026 it took a stake in NAiSE, a German maker of vendor-agnostic fleet-management software that lets AGVs/AMRs (autonomous mobile robots) from different brands and manual forklifts share one control layer.

Belgian startup founded in 2026 offering 'Humanoids-as-a-Service': factories pay a monthly fee and Motion handles robot selection, task training, data collection, IT integration, fleet management, financing and maintenance. Raised a $2M pre-seed led by Extantia (Aug 2026); five paid pilots in Belgian factories (loading crates, packing, conveyor placement).

French group that is Unitree's master distributor in Europe and acts as integrator: use-case assessment, robot selection, systems integration, functional safety, deployment and training. Runs one of Europe's first humanoid pilots in live car-parts manufacturing with Novares (2026), using Unitree humanoids.

Fraunhofer Institute for Manufacturing Engineering and Automation: applied research that brings robots into factories. In 2026 it launched an independent benchmark that tests humanoid robots (e.g. Unitree G1) on six industry criteria (energy efficiency, cleanroom fit, data security...), runs ROS 2-Industrial trainings, and is part of the euROBIN network.

Munich trade fair (Messe München) for robotics and automation, presented as the world's largest robotics portfolio across the value chain, focusing on Physical AI. Hosts munich_i with TUM's MIRMI institute (Hightech Summit, AI.Society show, Robothon developer challenge); publishes the automatica Trend Index survey (2026: 82% of German decision-makers want more humanoid subsidies).

Nordic early-stage VC. Led Sereact's €25M Series A (Jan 2025) and joined its $110M Series B (Apr 2026); co-led Machenta's $40M seed (Oct 2026), the largest UK robotics seed. One of the most active early backers of European robot-learning startups.
Transatlantic VC (San Francisco and Berlin). Led Sereact's $110M Series B (Apr 2026), Europe's 'robot brain' (Cortex 2) for warehouse and industrial picking.
AI-first early-stage VC run by Nathan Benaich, author of the yearly State of AI Report (covers robotics/embodied AI). Early and returning investor in Sereact (Series B, Apr 2026).
Venture/innovation arm of Exor's Lingotto Investment Management. Co-led RobCo's $100M Series C (Jan 2026) with Lightspeed, and was part of NEURA Robotics' €50M round (2023).

German multi-stage VC. Led ARX Robotics' €31M Series A (Apr 2025, military unmanned ground vehicles), co-invested in NEURA Robotics (2023) and is an existing investor in drone maker Quantum Systems ($1.2B round, Jul 2026).
Pan-European early-stage VC (>€1B AUM per mimic's release). Co-invested in mimic's $16M seed (Nov 2025, humanoid hands + physical-AI model) and led ARX Robotics' €11M Series A extension (Jul 2025).
French deep-tech VC. Led mimic robotics' $16M seed (Nov 2025) and is an investor in UK warehouse-robot company Dexory; Digital Venture Fund V reached €120M first close (Feb 2026).
Munich early-stage deep-tech VC. Co-led NEURA Robotics' €50M growth round in 2023 (with Primepulse, Lingotto and HV Capital).

UK deep-tech VC with repeated robotics deals: led Stateful Robotics' $4.8M pre-seed (Oxford spin-out, long-horizon robot planning, Mar 2026), led NEOintralogistics' €3M seed (warehouse robots-as-a-service, Jan 2026), investor in Slamcore (visual SLAM). Publishes the 'Capitalise' newsletter.
UK deep-tech VC. Co-led Gravis Robotics' $23M round (Nov 2025, autonomous excavator retrofit kits, ETH Zurich RSL spin-out) before SoftBank's $200M Series A made Gravis a unicorn (Aug 2026).

Construction- and infrastructure-tech VC backed by corporates such as Volvo Group VC, Holcim Maqer, Hilti and Trimble. Co-led Gravis Robotics' $23M round (Nov 2025); closed a $135M Fund II for AI, robotics and industrial tech (Nov 2026).
Founder-led European VC. Led Upside Robotics' $7.5M seed (agri robots, 2026) and the seed round of a European production-line robotics startup backed alongside PROTOTYPE (per tech.eu).

Paris-listed investment group. Its growth team led Dexory's £75M Series C (Oct 2025), part of a £124M raise for autonomous warehouse-scanning robots. Existing Dexory investors in that round included Atomico, Lakestar and Elaia.
Founder-built European VC. Existing investor in Dexory; published 'The Great Rollout' (24 Jun 2026), its thesis on European physical AI and robot deployment.

Global VC platform of Cathay Capital (Paris). Participated in THEKER's $85M Series A (Jun 2026, Europe's largest robotics Series A); closed a $1B vertical-AI fund (May 2025) whose corporate investors include Valeo, TotalEnergies, Groupe SEB and Groupe ADP.

EU public equity fund attached to the EIC Accelerator. Co-led Hyperion Robotics' $7.4M round (Jul 2026); its June 2026 EIC Accelerator package for Nanoflex Robotics (magnetically steered endovascular telerobotics) was €12.5M, of which €10M equity from the EIC Fund.
Multi-sovereign VC backed by 24 NATO allies. Existing investor in ARX Robotics (unmanned ground vehicles, Series A 2025); also backed Greenjets' $40M Series A.
Tech fund of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development. Led Nomagic's $44M Series B (Feb 2025; Polish AI picking robots) with Khosla Ventures and Almaz Capital.
Early-stage fund of Austrian investor Andreas Klinger, focused on robotics, physical AI and European tech sovereignty; launched Fund III in Jan 2026 (~€15M).

Swiss early-stage VC investing at the intersection of software and science. Backed Enact Intelligence's $30M pre-seed (Oct 2026; robot touch/dexterity, angels incl. Yann LeCun and Arthur Mensch); Enact is among the first deals of its new $250M Redalpine Capital VIII fund (closed Nov 2026).

German maker of 'cognitive' robots: collaborative arms (MAiRA, LARA), mobile platforms (MAV, MiPA) and the humanoid 4NE1. In Oct 2026 it launched 4NE1 Gen 4 (20% lighter, built for series production) and Neuron AI, its own multimodal foundation model (vision, touch, audio, robot state, language). With TUM it opened a €17M 'RoboGym' training centre near Munich airport. June 2026: Series C of up to $1.4B led by Tether (Amazon, Nvidia, Qualcomm, Bosch, Schaeffler, EIB also in); full disbursement depends on milestones per CNBC; valuation ~$7B per Bloomberg (not confirmed by NEURA).

Munich physical-AI company (DLR roots) making force-controlled robot arms (Diana 7, Thor series), the Agile Hand, mobile robotsand humanoids with legs or wheels (Agile ONE). Owns Franka Robotics since 2023. Nov 2026: raised $500M led by SoftBank (Nvidia, Hitachi, T.Capital) at an $8.5B valuation, ~$2B raised in total.

Maker of the Franka Research 3 (FR3), a 7-joint arm with torque sensors in every joint and 1 kHz low-level control: the 'reference' arm used in many robot-learning papers. Also sells FR3 Duo, a mobile FR3 and GELLO teleoperation kits. Founded 2016, part of Agile Robots since 2023.
props.Warm contact path: Public community forum and webinars on franka.de (no named contact)

props.What they build: Danish pioneer of collaborative robot arms ('cobots', arms safe enough to work next to people), part of US group Teradyne Robotics; 100,000+ deployments, payloads up to 35 kg. Sept 2026: launched Gen 7 (new g-Series arms, CB7 controller, PolyScope X software) designed for AI. March 2026: launched the UR AI Trainer imitation-learning data system with Scale AI.

One of the 'big four' industrial robot makers (founded 1898 in Augsburg, owned by China's Midea since 2016/17): industrial arms, AMRs and production systems; ~€3.9B sales, ~14,500 employees. In 2026 it partnered with Nvidia on 'Automation 2.0' (physical AI) and launched an AI 2D/3D vision system.

Robotics division of Swiss-Swedish ABB: industrial and collaborative arms, AMRs, controllers and software, 7,000+ employees. ABB agreed in Oct 2025 to sell it to SoftBank ($5.375B); on 5 Nov 2026 China blocked the deal for the China business, and ABB and SoftBank are discussing options. Its ownership may change.

ETH Zurich spin-off (2016) building ANYmal, a four-legged autonomous inspection robot for oil & gas, power and mining plants. Oct 2026: started deliveries of ANYmal X, certified for explosive atmospheres (ATEX/IECEx), first customers Equinor and DSM-Firmenich. Series B closed at $110M (Dec 2024); Opened an AI hub in Barcelona (2026).

Founded in Munich in 2020; builds modular robot arms sold 'robot-as-a-service' (no upfront investment) to small and mid-size factories, plus software (RobFlow, RobVision). Valuation doubled to over $1B in Oct 2026 (vs. January 2026) via a ~$40M round mostly buying employee shares (Sequoia, Lightspeed, Lingotto among investors); CEO Roman Hölzl relocated to the US (offices in Munich, Austin and San Francisco). Plans to launch 'Alfie', a two-armed mobile autonomous robot, in March 2027.

Barcelona robot maker since 2004 (offices in Toulouse and Bari) building research platforms: TIAGo and TIAGo Pro mobile manipulators (ROS 2, open-source software), the Kangaroo biped and TALOS humanoid, and a new 7-DoF arm with series elastic actuators (<10 kg, 3 kg payload) unveiled at ICRA 2026. Robots in 30+ countries.

Robotics division of Swedish measurement group Hexagon AB. Builds AEON, a wheeled-leg humanoid (165 cm, 60 kg, 2.4 m/s, 15 kg short-term payload, self-swapping battery, 5 h runtime) for manipulation, inspection and 3D 'reality capture'. Launched June 2025; piloted by Pilatus and Schaeffler; Schaeffler committed in April 2026 to deploy at least 1,000 AEONs by 2032.

UK maker of social humanoid robots for museums, events and research: Ameca (61 actuated degrees of freedom, cameras in the eyes, multilingual conversation via its Tritium AI/OS software), desktop versions (Ameca/Ami/Azi Desktop). Robots can be rented.

Founded 2015 in Gilching (Munich) by Florian Seibel; builds autonomous reconnaissance drones (unmanned aircraft) used heavily in Ukraine. Valuation went from €1B (Series C, May 2025) to $8B with a $1.2B Series D (July 2026).

UK surgical robotics company making Versius / Versius Plus, a compact, modular keyhole-surgery robot (FDA 510(k) cleared in the US). Oct 2026: Stryker invested ~$400M (preferred equity) with an exclusive option to acquire the company.

Barcelona startup building reconfigurable 'generalist' factory and logistics robots whose hands, arms and form can be swapped or resized per task (sorting packages, packing clothing...). June 2026: $85M Series A led by CRV (Samsung, Aglaé Ventures in), described as Europe's largest robotics Series A; showroom in central Barcelona.

Spin-off of the Italian Institute of Technology (IIT) led by Daniele Pucci (iCub/ergoCub/iRonCub lineage). Raised €70M (Dec 2025) to build 'Made in Italy' humanoids; its first humanoid GENE.01 has a touch- and proximity-sensing 'smart skin'.

ecosystem.name: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (IIT) – iCub Tech

props.What they build: Italian research institute that created iCub, an open-source (GPL) child-size humanoid (104 cm) with full-body touch skin. Also the ergoCub humanoid (Nature Machine Intelligence, July 2026) and the YARP middleware.

aliases: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (IIT) – iCub Tech

props.What they build: Estonian-founded (2014, HQ and engineering in Estonia, R&D in Helsinki) maker of sidewalk delivery robots: 10M+ autonomous deliveries with ~3,000 robots in 8 countries (2026). In 2026 it left many US campuses to focus on grocery and food retailers.

Alphabet's AI lab (HQ London). Builds the Gemini Robotics family: a vision-language-action model (VLA = a model that turns camera images + a text instruction into motor commands), an embodied-reasoning model for multi-step planning, and an on-device VLA. Gemini Robotics 2.5 (Nov 2026) reports 30-100% higher success than the previous version, tested on Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid and in a Mercedes-Benz factory pilot.

London-headquartered developer of end-to-end AI driving software: a learned system interprets sensor input and controls the vehicle. Its official site describes a mapless, sensor- and hardware-agnostic AI Driver and a Mercedes-Benz partnership. June 2026 reporting describes a planned London Uber robotaxi service, initially with safety operators and subject to regulatory approval, and a $1.2B February 2026 financing, with an additional $300M from Uber contingent on deployment. Its official announcements label the February financing Series D and add a $60M extension in April 2026.

Commercial AI platform and open-source community with Paris and New York connections. Its LeRobot library supports teleoperation, dataset collection, imitation/reinforcement-learning policy training and deployment; SO-101 and Reachy Mini provide accessible hardware options. LeRobot was co-founded by Rémi Cadène, who left Hugging Face in December 2025; June 2026 reporting identifies Steven Palma as its tech lead. October 2026 reporting describes Nvidia's proposed $12.9B acquisition as under DOJ scrutiny, with closing expected in H1 2027; completion is not established.
props.Warm contact path: Paris office; LeRobot Discord and GitHub community; LeRobot hackathon organizers

props.What they build: Frontier AI lab co-founded by Yann LeCun, with Paris among its locations. It develops world models that predict abstract representations of sensor data, helping an agent anticipate the consequences of actions and plan safely. Targets include industrial control, automation and robotics. March 2026 reporting confirms SBVA's €30M commitment to a seed round, alongside other investors; total round size is unknown from these opened sources.

Founded in early 2025; Reuters reports $105M raised and a June 2026 unveiling of Eno, a general-purpose robot with a wheeled base, foldable tower and human-like hands. Its May 2026 announcement introduces the proprietary GENE-26.5 foundation model and a data engine using human demonstrations, gloves and video; simulation supports development and evaluation. Targeted customer deployments were planned for the end of 2026. The company should not be treated as the sole originator of the earlier academic Genesis simulator.

Founded 2021 by Univ. of Stuttgart AI researchers. Hardware-agnostic 'robot brain' software: the Cortex foundation model takes natural-language instructions and outputs actions for arms, mobile manipulators and humanoids. Cortex 2.0 adds a world model that simulates candidate motions and scores them before acting. Raised $110M Series B (Apr 2026); April 2026 reporting names BMW, Daimler Truck, PepsiCo, Bol and Active Ants as customers.

Polish 'physical AI' for warehouse picking: its AI brain plus vision lets robot arms pick millions of different items. Zalando is rolling out up to 50 Nomagic robots across European fulfilment centres (Mar 2026), including a shoebox picker. Expanding in the US.

UK humanoid company building wheel-based industrial humanoids and the KinetIQ AI framework for fleet-level control and RL-based skill learning. Raised $152M Series A at $1.35B valuation (Jul 2026, led by Prime Movers Lab; Schaeffler, Bosch participate); total funding $270M; customer beta rollouts from Q4 2026.

Founded by former Nvidia researchers; builds a 'brain' for humanoids: low-level skills (walking, stairs, opening doors, carrying) trained in simulation with reinforcement learning, plus a higher-level model trained on human videos that picks which skill to run. Aims for one model deployable on any robot body. Raised a ~$50M Series A (Nov 2025, per press).

ETH Zurich spin-off doing end-to-end learning for dexterous manipulation (human-like robotic hands) in factories: assembly, kitting, cables, soft objects. In July 2026 introduced FLUX-mimic, a video-action model built with Black Forest Labs that learns tasks from video with far less demonstration data, deployed at Audi.

Robot-data startup founded by ex-Red Bull and Mercedes F1 engineers. Its Atlas platform records how humans and robots do real factory tasks (dedicated recording hardware + secure data platform) to train and deploy robots in production. Raised a $55M (≈€48M) seed in July 2026, described as Germany's largest; partners with Google Cloud.

Cloud infrastructure for robot learning: collect teleoperation demonstrations, curate/version datasets, train imitation and reinforcement-learning policies, and deploy/monitor them on real robots. Its SDK is open source. A November 2025 announcement describes free academic access, initially for selected universities with others potentially waitlisted; current eligibility and compute limits for 42AI are unknown. The same report confirms a $3M pre-seed led by Earlybird.
props.Warm contact path: Academic access enquiry via the platform; availability for 42AI is unknown

props.What they build: Open-source (MIT) data layer for physical AI: an SDK to log, store, query, visualize and stream multimodal robot data (cameras, point clouds, joint states) for debugging and training. Rerun Hub is the commercial catalog. Remote-first Swedish company; raised a $17M seed (Mar 2025, per press).

Robot programming software: NOVA, a robot-agnostic 'operating system' that connects digital twins/simulation (e.g. NVIDIA Isaac Sim) to real industrial robots so tasks can be designed in simulation and deployed the same day. Customers/partners reported include Volkswagen Sachsen and Schaeffler.

AI vision-and-control software MIRAI lets industrial robots adapt to changes in position, shape, lighting and reflective/transparent objects by learning from human demonstrations. Founded in Berlin by Ronnie Vuine; December 2024 reporting says the headquarters moved to San Francisco, rather than establishing a legal reorganization. Its official site still offers MIRAI; the last funding stage evidenced here is a $30M Series B announced in February 2022.

3D vision + hardware-agnostic AI software that lets existing industrial robots (FANUC, ABB, KUKA, Yaskawa, Comau, Universal Robots) see part positions and correct their motions in real time. Deployed on 200+ robots in 100+ factories (Stellantis, Toyota, Ford, Bosch). Raised $12.5M in Sept 2026 (total $34M).

Lausanne robotics startup whose September 2026 funding announcement names Faber VC as lead investor, with amount undisclosed. Combines task-specific AI, teleoperation data and soft robotic hardware for factory work such as kitting and cable handling. Its official site identifies AIR/AIR01, a wheeled humanoid, and two-arm cells sharing its software stack. The company describes learning on site with human supervision; its investor dates AIR's unveiling to 6 November 2026.

Paris startup developing hardware-agnostic AI software for industrial humanoid robots. The company says an operator can teach a task in under an hour with a few demonstrations; October 2026 reporting describes as few as ten demonstrations and a goal of shortening the full deployment process to one hour. Reported €5M pre-seed co-led by Contrarian Ventures and OVNI Capital. These are company claims and targets, rather than independently measured deployment guarantees.

ETH Zurich research lab led by Marco Hutter, developing legged robots and learning-based control for challenging environments. Its work includes ANYmal and the open-source RSL-RL library, which provides GPU-friendly reinforcement-learning algorithms such as PPO for robot-learning research.
European branch (led by Fraunhofer IPA) of the ROS-Industrial consortium, which extends ROS/ROS 2 open-source software to industrial robots; runs trainings and conferences for members.
props.Warm contact path: Public consortium contact: opensourcerobotics@ipa.fraunhofer.de (no personal introduction established)

props.City: La Roche-sur-Yon (2027: Parc Expo Les Oudairies)
props.What they build: France's national student robot contest (the French qualifier for Eurobot): teams design and build autonomous robots that play a yearly game on a table. 2026 edition ran 13-16 May 2026; 2027 edition is 5-8 May 2027 in La Roche-sur-Yon. Has Junior and 'Legends' categories.
props.Warm contact path: Organised by Planète Sciences; register a team on the official site.

props.What they build: International amateur robotics contest created in 1998 for students and young people; national organising committees run qualifiers (e.g. Coupe de France) and send teams to the Eurobot final. Also runs Eurobot Junior.
props.Warm contact path: Via Planète Sciences (French national committee, © Eurobot / Planète Sciences).

props.What they build: French youth science association that runs hands-on space, robotics and environment activities and organises the Coupe de France de Robotique and Eurobot.
props.Warm contact path: Contact via the Coupe de France / Planète Sciences national site.

props.What they build: European robotics association (industry + academia) behind the European Robotics Forum, the European Robotics Week, the European Robotics League and the euRobotics Awards.
props.Warm contact path: Through ERF attendance or a member lab/company.

props.What they build: Largest yearly meeting of the European robotics community (researchers, companies, EU officials) with workshops and an exhibition. ERF2026 was in Stavanger, ERF2027 is in Birmingham, ERF2028 in Athens.
props.Warm contact path: Registration open on eu-robotics.net (early bird until 1 Dec 2026).

props.What they build: Prizes handed out at ERF: TechTransfer Award, Renaud Champion Entrepreneurship Award, Georges Giralt PhD Award and Sustainability Leadership Recognition in Robotics.
Yearly week of public robotics outreach events (demos, open labs, school visits) coordinated by euRobotics across European countries.
props.Warm contact path: Register a local event on the euRobotics ERW page.

props.What they build: euRobotics competition series that benchmarks robots on realistic tasks (e.g. service, emergency, industrial scenarios); 2026 event ran 13-15 May 2026 in The Hague.

IEEE's flagship robotics conference, held in Europe in 2026, with 9 competitions: Robotic Grasping & Manipulation, What Bimanuals Can Do, RoboRacer, LeHome Challenge (garment manipulation skill learning in households), REAL-I (real-world embodied AI learning), AI for Robotic Surgery, BARN navigation, AgiBot World Challenge (embodied AI), Legged Robot Challenges.
props.Warm contact path: Follow each challenge's website from the ICRA competitions page.

props.What they build: Top single-track academic robotics conference (strong in robot learning); 2027 edition is in Europe.
World's largest industrial trade fair; hosts the ROBOTICS AWARD 2027 for applied robotics solutions, open also to non-exhibitors (entry fee 199 EUR + VAT, submitted via Alpha Awards).

Yearly KUKA competition for research/startup teams: finalists get a KUKA robot on loan, training and coaching; winner gets 20,000 EUR prize money. 2025 theme: Medical Robotics Challenge 2.0; 2026: Circular Packaging Challenge.
props.Warm contact path: Apply via the official KUKA call.

props.What they build: International intralogistics trade fair (warehouse robots, AMRs, automation).
French business event for IoT, AI, robotics and XR (8,015 professionals reported in 2026).
UK robotics and automation exhibition, now run together with IntraLogisteX.

props.City: Paris (2026: Jussieu, Sorbonne Université); 2025 joint FR+DE
props.What they build: French conference of the ROS (Robot Operating System) community; ROSCon FR 2026 ran 22-25 June 2026 at Jussieu (Sorbonne Université campus), Paris. A joint ROSCon FR + DE edition took place in 2025.
props.Warm contact path: Organisers announce on ROS Discourse; submit a talk/demo there.

props.What they build: CNRS national research network for French robotics labs: runs the biennial Journées du GdR (2026 edition), the JNRR doctoral school days, robotics PhD prizes and the Défi Transfert Robotique challenge.
RoboCup world championship (robot soccer, rescue, @Home service robots, industrial leagues, junior leagues) comes to Germany in 2027.
German open RoboCup tournament; 2026 edition ran 10-14 March 2026 in Cologne; German junior finals 9-12 March 2027 in Nuremberg.
French RoboCup committee running RoboCup Junior (soccer, rescue, onstage) and related qualifiers in France.

ETH Zurich-founded competition where people with disabilities complete everyday tasks using assistive tech (prosthetics, exoskeletons, wheelchairs, BCIs). Editions 2016, 2020, 2024; currently on a strategic pause (no next edition announced).
Field trial for unmanned ground robots (mule/transport, search-and-rescue/CASEVAC, reconnaissance); ELROB 2026 ran 15-19 June 2026 in Thun, run with Fraunhofer FKIE.
Hackathon/competition for robots in hazardous (nuclear) environments, held at a never-commissioned nuclear power plant; next edition 3-9 July 2027.
Space-robotics competition for student Mars-rover teams by the European Space Foundation; 2026: 124 registered teams from 29 countries, ~3,756 participants.
Robotics festival and competition founded 2001 (TalTech, Tallinn), running in 17+ countries with ~150,000 participants.
Student race-car competition whose Driverless Cup (DC) rewards autonomous racing cars; 2026 results published.
Global deep-tech startup competition with an 'Industrial AI & Novel Robotics' track and a 200,000 EUR Grand Prize; finalists pitch at the Hello Tomorrow Summit.
French national deep-tech innovation contest run by Bpifrance and the research ministry; 28th edition applications 25 Nov 2025 - 3 Feb 2026; winners get grants (up to 600 kEUR) for company creation.

ecosystem.name: AI for Good Global Summit and Robotics for Good Youth Challenge

aliases: AI for Good Global Summit and Robotics for Good Youth Challenge

props.What they build: EU network of excellence on AI-powered robotics that organises competitions, 'coopetitions' and hackathons between European labs.
French national skills competitions including mobile robotics and robot integration trades, feeding EuroSkills/WorldSkills.
Space-resources robotics challenge organised by ESA and ESRIC (Luxembourg).

props.Warm contact path: 42AI already co-hosted (via Hugging Face, in pilot map).

props.What they build: Humanoid-robot industry summit with editions in Silicon Valley, London, Tokyo and Seoul.
Physical-AI hackathon in Helsinki listed on Luma by Robotics Nation (registration closed).
Monthly Paris meetup of robotics enthusiasts (2,138 members on Meetup, 133 past events), plus online editions on Discord; e.g. 'Robot Party au Rendez-vous des Makers'.

UK robotics & autonomous systems academic network; runs events such as the UK-RAS Showcase (7 Jan 2027).
International agricultural-robotics forum with live in-field robot demos and the GOFAR tour (2026).
Global, student-driven competition for autonomous agricultural robots (field tasks in crop rows); 2027 edition takes place at the University of Lincoln, UK, in June 2027.

Bordeaux-based robotics team acquired by Hugging Face in April 2025. Builds Reachy Mini and Microduck; the latter is a 25 cm biped announced in August 2026 with an open-source software stack, but closed mechanical/electronic designs. Reachy products are already in the pilot and are not duplicated here.
props.Warm contact path: unknown; suggested public route: Pollen public contact via its official website

props.What they build: Inria/IRISA team on sensor-based and interactive robotics: visual servoing (controlling a robot from camera images), haptics, aerial and medical robots. Maintains ViSP, the open-source visual-servoing and tracking library.
Inria team (with CRIStAL / Univ. Lille) on soft and flexible robots made of deformable materials: modelling, simulation and control, built on the open-source SOFA simulation framework.
Inria / ENSTA team on developmental AI: curiosity-driven learning, autotelic agents and language-model agents, historically applied to robots (origin of the open-source Poppy robot platform).
Inria/LORIA team on life-long autonomy and interaction skills for robots in sensing environments (past projects ANDY, RESIBOTS on robots that adapt to damage with learning).

Inria Human-Centered Robotics team: humanoid and legged robots that work with people, learning and generative-AI methods for control of legged robots (partnership with UCL), open-source software and spin-offs.
Inria project team hosted at ENSC (Bordeaux INP) designing collaborative robots and robotic assistance for humans at work, mainly in industry (ergonomics, human-robot collaboration).
Inria team on cooperative and human-aware robot navigation in dynamic environments: multi-robot systems, human-centred robotics, perception and decision for autonomous agents.

Inria team developing intelligent, autonomous mobile robots that collaborate to achieve tasks in dynamic environments (perception, decision and control for multi-robot systems); runs public robotics seminars.

Autonomous-robotics research group of LaBRI (Univ. Bordeaux, ENSEIRB-MATMECA, CNRS). Builds small humanoids for RoboCup (SigmaBan) and agricultural robots; released Microban, a fully 3D-printable open-source humanoid (Raspberry Pi Zero 2W + 19 Dynamixel servos).
~80-person department combining microrobotics, mechatronics, control and data science (robots and actuators at micro scale).
CNRS/Univ. Poitiers/ISAE-ENSMA physics and engineering lab; includes robotics and human-machine interaction work (e.g. a painting robot).
Versailles systems-engineering lab; team Robotique Interactive (RI) on assistance and interaction robots.
Évry lab in computing, integrative biology and complex systems; robotics work incl. a 2026 PhD on distributed real-time control architectures for humanoid robots and WRC SARA 2026 best student paper.
Amiens lab in computer science, control, robotics and computer vision; domain 'Perception robotique' (robotic perception).
Arts et Métiers lab on physical and digital systems engineering; part of the TIRREX robotics research infrastructure and active in the GdR Robotique.
CESI's digital-innovation research lab for industry and learning; listed by GdR Robotique (industry-of-the-future robotics, cobotics).
French aerospace research centre; its information-processing & systems department covers robotics and autonomy (mini-drones/UAVs, ground and underwater robots, piloting aids).
Lille computer-science and control research centre (CNRS, Univ. Lille, Centrale Lille); hosts robotics/control teams and partners with Inria DEFROST.
Lyon lab (INSA Lyon, Centrale Lyon, Univ. Lyon 1) on electrical engineering and control; its medical-robotics activity covers medico-surgical gestures, teleoperation, haptics and visual servoing.
French national ocean research institute; listed by GdR Robotique as a robotics lab (underwater/marine robotics).
Corporate AI research lab of NAVER: AI for robotics (vision, action, interaction, HRI), 3D vision models such as the open DUSt3R, human body models (Anny), regular public seminars.
Technological research institute for manufacturing (aero, naval, energy, rail); transversal expertise in robotics & cobotics to deploy robots in complex industrial environments.

France 2030 priority research programme on 'organic robotics' (robots socially adapted to humans and their environment): 3 scientific challenges, 7 targeted projects, €34M budget, ~70 PhD students; the national robotics research umbrella.
Mechanical/industrial engineering school; LISPEN lab; student robotics clubs on several campuses (teams akimbot and Robrag'ss from Lille, robobobo) at the Coupe de France de Robotique.
Digital engineering school of Institut Polytechnique de Paris; its student club Télécom Robotic competes at the Coupe de France de Robotique.
Research-oriented school; hosts Centre Borelli (applied maths, vision, data and robotics research) and the LURPA production-engineering lab.
Largest research university of the Paris region; umbrella of many robotics labs (LISV, IBISC, LISN...) and robotics masters.
Engineering institute (Phelma, Ense3, Ensimag...); robotics clubs Robotronik (Phelma) and Polybot Grenoble; GIPSA-lab partner.
Engineering school partner of IRISA/Inria Rennes; its club robot competes at the Coupe de France.
Engineering school (mechatronics); Club de Robotique de l'INSA de Strasbourg (CRIS); ICube partner.

Industrial arms, collaborative CRX robots, CNC automation and ROBOGUIDE robot simulation. The current product page includes 2024-2026 controller and physical-AI updates.

props.What they build: aibo companion robots combine sensing, expressive motion and cloud-supported behavior. A developer program is linked from the live aibo site; this does not make the robot open hardware.
Honda Robotics researches avatar robots and UNI-ONE mobility assistance. Its official strategy explicitly moves beyond a single general-purpose ASIMO-style humanoid toward task-specific assistance.

Japan-based Toyota develops the Human Support Robot (HSR), a mobile arm for domestic assistance. The cited 2015 developer-community program is historical, not evidence that a French student lab can borrow an HSR today. Toyota Research Institute in the US is not this row.

Develops AI chips, computing infrastructure and AI applications, with industrial-robot partners among its shareholders. Spun out Preferred Robotics; the latter now builds Kachaka products. PFR reports joint development of PLaMo-SemGround for indoor mobile-robot scene understanding in September 2026, not a verified public model release.

PFN spin-off building small autonomous mobile robots: Kachaka Pro, Kachaka Evo and the HAPiiBOT floor-cleaning robot co-developed with Amano. Publishes a Kachaka Python/ROS 2 API SDK; hardware and the full autonomy stack are not thereby open-source.
props.Warm contact path: unknown; the official Kachaka API GitHub Discussions is a public technical route, not a warm introduction.

props.What they build: Builds teachless robot controllers and MujinOS, combining perception, motion planning and no-code orchestration for factories and warehouses. Japan-founded business, distinct from the US subsidiary whose website supplies the cited corporate history. Its opened official news index documents a Series C in September 2023 and a $233M raise in December 2025; the Japan site independently confirms manufacturing/logistics deployments.
props.Warm contact path: Corporate history verifies Mujin Europe opened in Eindhoven in October 2023; approach through the official company contact, not a known personal introduction.

props.What they build: Develops AI-driven and remotely operated manipulation systems. Its September 2025 announcement documents TX Ghost beverage-restocking pilots at select Tokyo 7-Eleven stores; its 2026 site discusses humanoids and robot foundation-model development.

Develops collaborative picking AMRs, automated storage/retrieval systems and multi-robot control. Its live site includes customer warehouse case studies and 2024-2026 product news; performance claims are vendor claims, not independent comparisons.

Kawada group company building NEXTAGE dual-arm industrial humanoids, including NXA and Fillie, plus OPEN research variants with extensible software. Also lists HRP-2/3/4 research platforms. A humanoid upper body does not imply bipedal walking.

Japan national research institute; its humanoid group developed HRP-5P for heavy manipulation such as gypsum-board installation. The 2018 prototype is a historical research platform, not evidence of a current commercial offering.

University robotics laboratory researching integrated perception/action, assistive humanoids, musculoskeletal robots such as Kengoro and aerial robots. Its research index also lists open-source robot software. Classified as School to represent the university/laboratory entry together, not as a second duplicate university row.

Biennial robot exhibition at Tokyo Big Sight spanning production robots, service robots and components. The live site reports the 2025 show and says the next iREX is scheduled for early December 2027; RoboNext 2026 is a separate event.
Industry association publishing Japanese robot statistics and membership information, and linking to robot exhibitions. Its English site has quarterly statistics through July-September 2026.

Volunteer ROS community organizing developer meetings, study sessions, workshops and hackathons. Its official GitHub profile links connpass, Slack and organizer contact details; it is not the builder of ROS itself.
props.Warm contact path: unknown; official GitHub profile links community Slack, connpass and the public organizer email. These are cold outreach channels.

props.What they build: Investment holding group with documented participation in Telexistence's 2023 Series B. The same announcement distinguishes SoftBank Group as investor from SoftBank Robotics Group as a strategic business partner; no Pepper/NAO builder attribution is inferred.

Self-balancing exoskeletons (Atalante X used at 150+ clinical and research sites; Eve personal exoskeleton) and, since 2025, the Calvin-40 industrial humanoid developed with Renault. Opened a robot production site in Paris.

Mirokaï social robots (Miroki and Miroka): manga-style robots with a head and two arms riding on a motorised ball, deployed in hospitals, nursing homes, hotels and Lyon airport. Founded 2021 by ex-Aldebaran Jérôme Monceaux; Google DeepMind Gemini trusted tester.

Lightweight, low-cost general-purpose humanoid robots (Northstar design, Version 0 prototype, designed and assembled in Paris). Co-founded by Rémi Cadène, ex-Tesla Optimus and former lead of Hugging Face LeRobot.
props.Warm contact path: Via the Hugging Face LeRobot team (Cadène's former team)

props.What they build: French LLM company that entered robotics in July 2026 with Robostral Navigate, an 8B single-camera navigation model trained on simulated data with RL; organised a Physical AI & Robotics hackathon in Paris (April 2025) with Hugging Face LeRobot.
Synthetic data platform for physical AI: describe a 3D scene, vary it millions of ways and get perfect ground truth for training robot/vision models. Raised $10M seed (Inovia) in Nov 2026.
Autonomous robots for existing (brownfield) warehouses: picking, sorting, palletizing, container unloading, packing. Founded 2025; Station F Future 40 2025.
Modular warehouse robotics: TAK-ONE system that slides parcels and bins horizontally and vertically across levels (compact buffer/sorting). €10M round in 2025 (Supernova Invest, Bpifrance).
3D LiDAR SLAM software (Exwayz Engine): mapping, centimetre localization and perception for robots and autonomous vehicles, CPU-only. CentraleSupélec 21st accelerator; €1M raised.
Microrobots the size of a grain of rice that travel inside the brain for minimally invasive neurosurgery. Founded 2017 in Paris; based at AP-HP Hôtel-Dieu; $28M raised in 2025.
Maestro surgical-assistant robot for laparoscopy (holds and moves instruments for the surgeon); 2026 software update turned it into a 'physical AI' platform. Backed by Sofinnova and Cathay Health.
Marker-less robotic assistant for total knee arthroplasty (orthopaedic surgery), under development (not yet cleared).
Swan: robot that captures standardized full-body dermoscopic skin images for early skin-cancer detection. Raised $18M in 2026 (Sonder Capital, Deeptech 2030 Fund).

AI-piloted autonomous drones (interceptors, strike and reconnaissance), radar/EW payloads and command software. Founded 2024, French defence unicorn; $200M Series B led by Dassault Aviation (Jan 2026).
Modular autonomous underwater vehicles (low-cost subsea drone swarms) for fleet defence. Founded 2025; Y Combinator P26; Station F Future 40 2026.
Real-time low-latency (≈8 ms) infrastructure for robot teleoperation, monitoring, training-data collection and human takeover; founded by VLC lead developer Jean-Baptiste Kempf; open-source strategy.
Agentic 'common brain' / OS that orchestrates fleets of heterogeneous robots and devices through natural language.
Teaching infrastructure that trains existing robot models on customer-specific jobs they fail at (XR + 3D computer vision).
Collaborative robots for industrial sanding/finishing; CEA-List spin-off; €7M raised in Feb 2026.
Autonomous forklift robots (AGV/AMR hybrids with LiDAR navigation) built on OEM chassis; 2025 sales €31.4M.
Goods-to-person warehouse robots (mobile robots carrying shelves to pickers); founded 2013, HQ and R&D in Paris.
Outdoor logistics robots (autonomous car-parking/vehicle-moving robots); founded 2015, HQ Paris.
Continues NAO (and Aldebaran legacy) development after Maxvision bought Aldebaran's core assets in July 2025; social humanoids for research, education and healthcare.
Drones, now mainly professional/defence micro-UAVs such as ANAFI UKR (sovereign ISR micro-drone, 2025).
Event-based (neuromorphic) vision sensors and software: cameras that only report pixel changes, giving very low latency perception for robots and drones.
Infrastructure-based physical AI: 3D LiDAR software that tracks people/vehicle flows in airports, factories and cities.
Maritime robotics (drones/underwater vehicles) and inertial navigation systems; high-tech industrial group.
Car maker; strategic investor in Wandercraft and first customer for its Calvin-40 humanoid for factory tasks.
IT/engineering services group; tests Unitree robots with Orano for operations in radioactive zones.
Aircraft maker; led Harmattan AI's $200M Series B (Jan 2026) to back autonomous drones.
World's largest startup campus; hosts Genesis AI, Bleu Robotics, Marso, AICE (Future 40), MACHINA physical-AI summit and GOSIM robotics hackathon.

props.What they build: Makes collaborative robot arms and automation solutions. P3020 is a five-axis palletizing arm that moves boxes onto pallets, with 30 kg payload and 2,030 mm reach. Its public doosan-robot2 ROS 2 packages expose robot control and simulation integration; open software does not mean open robot hardware.
props.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: sales.robotics@doosan.com or the official ROS 2 repository issue tracker for a specific technical question.

props.What they build: KAIST spin-out building robot platforms. RB-Y1 combines two seven-joint arms with a wheeled base for manipulation, teleoperation, and whole-body-control research. Provides Python/C++ SDK and simulation assets. Samsung announced its 35% stake and subsidiary consolidation in December 2024; this does not make the hardware open source.
props.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: official RB-Y1 support channel or an SDK issue/discussion, backed by a concrete reproducible demo.

props.What they build: Builds DYNAMIXEL smart actuators and open research platforms: TurtleBot3, OMX entry-level arms, OMY manipulators, AI Worker mobile manipulators, and AI Sapiens humanoids. Physical AI Tools links ROS 2 robot control to LeRobot demonstration datasets and policy training. This is the strongest direct software bridge to 42AI in the shortlist; actual landed hardware prices remain unknown.
props.Warm contact path: unknown personal connection; public route: ROBOTIS Discourse forum and a useful Physical AI Tools GitHub issue/PR, then its global contact form.

props.What they build: Korean wearable/humanoid startup. Sells WIM walking-assistance devices and develops ALLEX upper-body humanoid hardware for compliant, dexterous manipulation. Announced KRW 95 billion Series B in May 2026. Its BSD-licensed ALLEX simulation model is public; the repository calls physical hardware research-prototype v2 with limited research-edition access planned later in 2026, not a mass-market robot.
props.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: official contact form, ALLEX model repository, or an introduction via investor FuturePlay.

props.What they build: NAVER research organization building ARC cloud robotics: cloud-side robot management, localization, and a web operating layer. Builds and tests Rookie delivery robots and AMBIDEX dual-arm manipulation, connecting a heterogeneous robot fleet in NAVER 1784. An April 2025 official account reports about 100 robots and over 60,000 deliveries; these are company-reported historical figures.
props.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: NAVER LABS research enquiry or public conference speakers; no existing 42AI connection verified.

props.What they build: University with multiple robotics groups. Its DRCD Lab builds HOUND quadrupeds with custom drivetrains and learned locomotion; HOUND 1 used a reinforcement-learning controller for its 2023 speed demonstration. HOUND 2 is a newer lab platform, but its official page gives conflicting mass figures. This row represents the university; the lab is a contact route, not a duplicate organization.
props.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: DRCD lab contact at its official KAIST site, or a specific corresponding author with a reproducible research question.

ecosystem.name: Korea Institute of Robotics & Technology Convergence (KIRO)

props.What they build: Government-backed specialised robotics research institute (founded 2005 as Pohang Intelligent Robot Institute, reorganised as KIRO in 2012) located on the POSTECH campus in Pohang. Develops underwater/construction, medical-service, safety and agricultural robots and runs demonstration centres (safety-robot and agricultural-robot test centres) plus training programmes for industry. Specific current platforms and 2026 activity are unknown: the official site kiro.re.kr was unreachable during verification.
props.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: KIRO international contact or RoTIC education enquiry. No Paris exchange or free training eligibility verified.

props.What they build: Deep-tech venture investor providing early-stage funding and company-building support. props.What they build: Seoul startup rooted in Seoul National University AI research. Co-developed CLIP-RT, a one-billion-parameter vision-language-action model (camera images and instructions to robot motions), with public code and checkpoints. In 2026 presented HABILIS Brain 0 and a stack for data, training, deployment, and robot operations. Funding stage is unknown; an investment target is not a completed round.

props.What they build: Provides GPU and Jetson computing plus the Isaac robotics stack. Isaac Sim simulates robots and sensors; Isaac Lab adds workflows for training robot policies, including reinforcement learning (learning through trial and reward).
Develops the Optimus general-purpose humanoid program and AI for perception and robot control. Public program descriptions are not proof of unsupervised commercial deployment.

Builds and operates warehouse automation, including Proteus mobile robots, Sparrow picking arms and the tactile Vulcan system. Amazon's own fulfillment network provides a concrete customer and integration environment, unlike a staged home demo.

Builds Spot for mobile inspection, Stretch for warehouse case handling, and Atlas for industrial humanoid work. These are different products and should not be treated as one general-purpose deployment.
Builds robot-assisted surgical and bronchoscopy systems, including da Vinci. These assist trained clinical teams; they are not autonomous surgeons or appropriate beginner hardware.

Builds Figure humanoids and Helix embodied AI. Its homepage presents Figure 03 for home assistance. In September 2025 it announced more than $1B of committed Series C capital at a $39B post-money valuation; committed funding is not revenue or evidence of deployment scale.

Develops generalist robot policies in the pi family. A vision-language-action model turns camera images and instructions into robot actions. Its site provides pi0 code/weight releases and later models; Axios reported a $600M round in November 2025, but the opened article did not label its series.

Develops Skild Brain, a robot-control model intended to work across different robot bodies. Its January 2026 announcement reports $1.4B raised at a valuation above $14B; claims that it can control any robot remain company claims, not independently established guarantees.

Builds Digit humanoids and Arc fleet software for industrial automation. Its September 2025 NVIDIA collaboration page confirms Series C investment and use of Isaac Lab for sim-to-real robot learning; its homepage identifies Salem as Digit's assembly location.

Builds Apollo humanoids for manufacturing and logistics. February 2026's company release reports more than $935M in total Series A financing and partnerships with Mercedes-Benz, GXO, Jabil and Google DeepMind. Apollo 2 is already in the pilot robot/model file and is not recreated here.
